# GAME BASIC for SEGA SATURN: Sample Programs

This book collects every sample program that comes with GAME BASIC for SEGA SATURN (ASCII Corp., Bits Laboratory and ESP inc., 1998) in one place, in English. It is meant for learning how to write your own games: each program has a short description of what it does and which techniques it shows, followed by its listing.

It covers the 67 programs on the GAME BASIC CD, the three sample programs that come with the DXFCONV converter on the Windows 95 tools CD, and the program listings printed in the Tutorial Manual and the Reference Manual.

> **About the translation.** The programs' comments and on-screen text were written in Japanese, mostly in half-width katakana. Here they are translated into English inside the listings, so a listing is no longer byte-for-byte the file on the CD: English text is a different length, so some screens will not line up as they did, and the Japanese font codes some programs print are gone. The line numbers and all of the code are exactly as on the CD. To run a program, load the original from the CD.

## 1. How to read this book

### Running a sample

On the Saturn, start the launcher (it starts by itself when GAME BASIC boots, or press Shift+F1), pick a file and press A. Or type the name yourself:

```
LOAD "CD:G_MOBIL.B",R
```

`FILES "CD:"` lists the files on the CD. A few programs need a particular controller (the Virtua Gun, Shuttle Mouse, Racing Controller, Mission Stick or Multi-Terminal 6); the descriptions say so.

To read a program on a PC, the CD's files are in `GAME_BASIC/GAME_BASIC_CD/GAME_BASIC_files.zip` in this project. `.B` files are plain text in the Shift-JIS character set, with CR+LF line ends, so any editor that understands Shift-JIS opens them. The VS Code extension in `vscode-game-basic` highlights them.

### How the listings are shown

- **Line numbers** are the program's own. Many samples number from 1000 up; jumps in the numbers are as on the CD.
- **Comments and strings** that were in Japanese are translated in place. Comments begin with `'` or `REM`. Strings are the text between `"` marks. English kept from the original is unchanged.
- **Long runs of `DATA`** are left out. Most of the bytes on the CD are data: polygon models, textures, music, FM tones. When six or more `DATA` lines come together, the listing shows the first three and the last one, and puts a line like this in place of the rest:

  ```
        ' ... 2,920 DATA lines not shown (lines 5000-7930) ...
  ```

  These marker lines are not part of the program. Labels (`*NAME`) inside a data block are always kept, so you can see where each `RESTORE` points. The heading of each program gives the full size and how many lines are shown.
- **Variants.** Where a program is a small change to another one (for example `G_JUMP_A.B`, which is `G_JUMP.B` for the analogue pad), the listing shows only the differences, as a "diff": lines starting `-` are in the original, lines starting `+` replace them, and the `@@` lines mark where each change is. Line numbers are left off in a diff, because the variants are renumbered.
- **The first line.** Several samples start with an unnumbered line such as `LOAD"COM:D"`. It was left over from sending the program from a PC, and `LOAD` ignores a line with no number.

### Patterns you will see again and again

The samples were written by several teams, but they share a few habits that are worth knowing before you read them:

- **"Object Item Number" constants.** Most 3D programs begin by naming the items of the `OBJ` array: `TYPE = 0: FLAG = 1`, `XP = 4` (position), `XR = 8` (rotation), `XS = 12` (scale), `ATR = 16`, `POLYGON = 17`, `PARENT = 20`, `XV = 24` (speed), `XRV = 36` (rotation speed) and so on. Then `OBJ(1,XP) = x,y,z` sets three items at once. GAME BASIC also has the built-in names `@XP`, `@TYPE` and so on, which later programs use instead.
- **Labels instead of line numbers.** `GOSUB *SETUP` and `GOTO *LOOP` jump to labels, so the programs can be renumbered freely.
- **A main loop of subroutine calls.** `*MAIN: GOSUB *MOVE: GOSUB *CHECK: ... GOTO *MAIN`. Each subroutine does one job.
- **Timer interrupts.** `ON INTERVAL (0) GOSUB *CLOCK` and `INTERVAL (0) ON,1` run a subroutine every frame (1/60 s), used for clocks, fades and reading pads while the main program does something else.
- **Pad bits.** `P = PAD(0,1)` reads pad 1 as a bit mask; `IF P AND @PAD_A THEN ...` tests one button.
- **Fades.** `COLOROFS (FADE,FADE,FADE)` with a value stepping between -255 and 0 fades the screen out and in.
- **Housekeeping at the start.** `SKCLOSE` closes the software keyboard, `KLOAD ON` loads the kanji font, `CLEAR ,1360` reserves the file buffer that `TARG` needs, `PLAYINIT` sets up sound.
- **Passing values between programs.** The music menus `POKE` a few bytes of user memory before running another program with `LOAD ... ,R` and `PEEK` them when control comes back.

## 2. A path for learning to write a game

You do not need to read the book in order. If your aim is to write a game, this order builds up one idea at a time:

| Step | Read | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tutorial Manual examples (chapter 7) | Read the short listings from the manuals first: they introduce lines, loops, subroutines, arrays, sprites and a first polygon one idea at a time. |
| 2 | `P_CLOCK.B`, `P_PFONT.B`, `P_FLOWER.B`, `P_NEKO.B` (chapter 4) | One graphics idea each: polygon fonts, parent-child objects, textures and sprites. |
| 3 | `G_MOBIL.B` (chapter 3) | The smallest complete 3D game, with a line-by-line explanation in the Tutorial Manual (TM section 2.8). |
| 4 | `G_BOMB.B` and `G_HATA.B` (chapter 3) | How a game loop is organised as a list of subroutines, and how `ON INTERVAL` reads the pads in the background. |
| 5 | `G_MAZE.B` and `G_JUMP.B` (chapter 3) | Bigger 3D games: generating a level, building it from polygons, simple physics and custom music. |
| 6 | `G_SABA.B`, `G_THESEU.B`, the `BOU` files and `G_TEKE.B` (chapter 3) | Full games: light-gun input, stage data in files, programs split across several files, saving progress. |
| 7 | `S_TUTOR.B` (chapter 5) | When you are ready to add music and sound effects: a complete MML course, now in English. |

After that, the graphics demos in chapter 4 are a toolbox: each shows one feature in a few dozen lines. The tool programs in chapter 6 show how to build bigger interfaces (windows, menus, mouse input), and chapter 5 has music you can reuse, notably the Lunar version A tunes, which were laid out to be used as game BGM.

The English User Guide (`GAME_BASIC_for_SEGA_SATURN_User_Guide_EN`) explains the commands these programs use, and the translated Tutorial and Reference Manuals give the full detail.

### G_MOBIL.B: Mobil

**File:** `G_MOBIL.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 6,220 bytes, 217 lines. 182 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_MOBIL.B",R`.

A 3D driving game. You steer a vehicle over a chequered field and touch the pylons in order before time runs out. The Tutorial Manual's chapter on making a game (TM section 2.8) explains this listing block by block, so read the two together.

**Techniques:**

- `PAD(0,1)` read as a bit mask and tested with the `@PAD_...` constants
- Steering with a viewing direction, speed and acceleration, using `XSIN`/`XCOS` to move in the direction you face
- A ground built from character BG tiles with `PUTCHR`
- Pylon objects built with `SETVERTEX`/`SETPOLYGON` from `DATA`, placed at random on a map array
- Simple distance test for touching a pylon, a countdown timer, and `BGM`/`EFFECT` for music and sound effects

> Start here. It is the smallest complete 3D game on the CD.

```
LOAD "COM:D"
 1000 SCREEN 5,4,256:SKCLOSE
 1001 '----------------------------------
 1002 'BGM & sound effects set
 1003 PLAYINIT "EXTRA4"
 1004 EFFECT 1,0,"@10 %1 C"  :'SONG#1=BGM1
 1005 EFFECT 2,0,"@9  %1 C"  :'SONG#2=BGM2
 1006 EFFECT 3,0,"@11 %1 C"  :'SONG#3=BGM3
 1007 EFFECT 4,0,"@7C"       :'SONG#4 = pylon touch sound
 1008 '----------------------------------
 1010 PRIORITY 4,7
 1020 '----------------------------------
 1030 SETPERS 60
 1040 SETLIGHT 1,1,.5,RGB(29,29,31),RGB(0,0,8)
 1050 SETDISP 7
 1060 ROTCENTER 0,0,15
 1070 ROTPOS 128*8,128*8,15
 1080 BANK=-.25:ROTATE BANK
 1090 DIM MAP(64,64)
 1100 DIM POALX(9),POALY(9)
 1110 '----------------------------------
 1120 A$=READCHR$(4,0,256)
 1130 SETCHR 8,0,A$
 1140 PALETTE 8,1,RGB(10,10,10)
 1150 PALETTE 8,15,RGB(10,10,30)
 1160   FOR GX= 0 TO 15
 1170     FOR GY = 0 TO 15
 1180       FOR X = 0 TO 3
 1190         FOR Y = 0 TO 3
 1200           PUTCHR 8,((GX*8)+X,(GY*8)+Y),135*2
 1210           PUTCHR 8,((GX*8)+4+X,(GY*8)+4+Y),135*2
 1220         NEXT
 1230       NEXT
 1240     NEXT
 1250   NEXT
 1260 CCOPY 8,(0,0)-(127,127) TO 8,(0,128)
 1270 CCOPY 8,(0,0)-(127,127) TO 8,(128,0)
 1280 CCOPY 8,(0,0)-(127,127) TO 8,(128,128)
 1290 '----------------------------------
 1300 SETVERTEX  0,16,READ
 1310 SETPOLYGON 0,8,0,READ
 1320 SETATR     0,8,READ
 1330 SETVERTEX  1,4,READ
 1340 SETPOLYGON 1,1,1,READ
 1350 SETATR     1,1,READ
 1360 '----------------------------------
 1370   FOR X=0 TO 64
 1380     FOR Y=0 TO 64
 1390       MAP(X,Y)= 0
 1400     NEXT
 1410   NEXT
 1420 OBJ(0,@ORDER) = 6
 1430   FOR P = 1 TO 8
 1440 *GEN_POAL
 1450     X = (RND(56)+4)
 1460     Y = (RND(56)+4)
 1470     IF MAP(X,Y)<>0 THEN *GEN_POAL
 1480     MAP(X,Y) = 1
 1490     X = X * 32
 1500     Y = Y * 32
 1510     POALX(P) = X
 1520     POALY(P) = Y
 1530 '
 1540     OBJ(P,@ATR)   = 0,0
 1550     OBJ(P,@XP)    = X,,-Y
 1560     OBJ(P,@ORDER) = 0
 1570 '
 1580     OBJ(P+8,@ATR)   = 1,1
 1590     OBJ(P+8,@TYPE)  = 4
 1600     OBJ(P+8,@XP)    = X,,-Y
 1610     OBJ(P+8,@XRV)   = 0,-.005
 1620     OBJ(P+8,@ORDER) = 0
 1630 '
 1640     SETPFONT P+16,48+P,(.5,.5,.2),RGB(15,15,15)
 1650     OBJ(P+16,@XR)    = ,RND(10)/10
 1660     OBJ(P+16,@XRV)   = 0,.008
 1670     OBJ(P+16,@XP)    = X,-104,-Y
 1680     OBJ(P+16,@ORDER) = 0
 1690   NEXT
 1700 *RESET_TERGET
 1710 TERGET = 1
 1720   FOR P = 1 TO 8
 1730     OBJ(P,@TYPE)  = 4
 1740   NEXT
 1750 '----------------------------------
 1760 ROTOVER 1,240*2
 1770 PX=0:PY=0:PZ=15
 1780 DIR     = .375        :'Viewing direction
 1790 PVY     = 0           :'Player X speed
 1800 PVX     = 0           :'Player Y speed
 1810 PVA     = .025        :'Player acceleration parameter
 1820 BRK     = .02         :'Deceleration parameter
 1830 DIR_PRM = .003
 1840 F=0
 1850 TIME = 0
 1860 START = 0
 1870 BGM 1:LOCATE 14,10:PRINT "PRESS START  "
 1880 *LOOP
 1890 IF START = 1 THEN *SKIP_STT
 1900 PDL = PAD(0,1)
 1910 IF PDL AND @PAD_START THEN BGM 2:GOTO *GAME_START
 1920 GOTO *SKIP_MOVE
 1930 *GAME_START
 1940 LOCATE 14,10:PRINT "              "
 1950 LOCATE  8,12:PRINT "                   "
 1960 START = 1
 1970 '
 1980 *SKIP_STT
 1990 DY = ABS(POALY(TERGET)-PY)
 2000 IF DY > 10 THEN *NO_TOUCH
 2010 DX = ABS(POALX(TERGET)-PX)
 2020 IF DX > 10 THEN *NO_TOUCH
 2030 EFFECT -4  :'Pylon touch
 2040 OBJ(TERGET+0,@TYPE) = 0
 2050 TERGET = TERGET + 1
 2060 IF TERGET = 9 THEN *GAME_END
 2070 '
 2080 *NO_TOUCH
 2090 '
 2100 PDL = PAD(0,1)
 2110 '
 2120 IF PDL AND @PAD_LEFT  THEN DIR = DIR - DIR_PRM
 2130 IF DIR < 0 THEN DIR = DIR + 1
 2140 IF PDL AND @PAD_RIGHT THEN DIR = DIR + DIR_PRM
 2150 IF DIR > 1 THEN DIR = DIR - 1
 2160 '
 2170 SIDE = PVX*XCOS(DIR)-PVY*XSIN(DIR)
 2180 SX = -SIDE*XCOS(DIR)*.01
 2190 SY = SIDE*XSIN(DIR)*.01
 2200 PVX=PVX+SX
 2210 PVY=PVY+SY
 2220 '
 2230 AX=PVA*XCOS(DIR)
 2240 AY=-PVA*XSIN(DIR)
 2250 IF PDL AND @PAD_R THEN PVX=PVX+AX: PVY=PVY+AY
 2260 IF PDL AND @PAD_L THEN PVX=PVX-AX: PVY=PVY-AY
 2270 '
 2280 AX=PVA*XSIN(DIR)
 2290 AY=PVA*XCOS(DIR)
 2300 IF PDL AND @PAD_A THEN PVX=PVX+AX: PVY=PVY+AY
 2310 IF PDL AND @PAD_B THEN PVX=PVX-PVX*BRK:PVY=PVY-PVY*BRK
 2320 IF PDL AND @PAD_C THEN PVX=PVX-AX: PVY=PVY-AY
 2330 '
 2340 PX=PX+PVX:PY=PY-PVY
 2350 '
 2360 TIME = TIME + .0167
 2370 MIN = INT(TIME/60)
 2380 SEC = TIME-INT(TIME/60)*60
 2390 LOCATE 1,20:PRINT USING "##:##.##";MIN,SEC
 2400 IF TIME > 300 THEN *TIME_OUT
 2410 '
 2420 *SKIP_MOVE
 2430 F=F+.005
 2440 IF F > 1 THEN F = 0
 2450 FZ = .5*XSIN(F)
 2460 '
 2470 ROTPOS PX,PY,PZ+FZ
 2480 ROTATE,,DIR
 2490 OBJ(0,@YR) = -DIR
 2500 OBJ(0,@XP) = -PX,PZ+FZ,PY
 2510 VSYNC
 2520 GOTO *LOOP
 2530 '
 2540 *GAME_END
 2541 BGM 3
 2550 LOCATE 1,20:PRINT "        "
 2560 LOCATE 14,10:PRINT "FINISH !!"
 2570 LOCATE  8,12:PRINT USING "CLEAR TIME ##:##.##";MIN,SEC
 2580 VSYNC 180
 2590 GOTO *RESET_TERGET
 2600 *TIME_OUT
 2601 PLAYFADE 0,0,4
 2610 LOCATE 1,20:PRINT "        "
 2620 LOCATE 14,10:PRINT "TIME OUT !!"
 2630 VSYNC 180
 2640 GOTO *RESET_TERGET
 2650 '----------------------------------
 2660 DATA  -2, -64, -2
 2670 DATA   2, -64, -2
 2680 DATA   2, -64, -2
      ' ... 34 DATA lines and 1 comment line not shown (lines 2690-3030) ...
 3040 DATA (4, 1, 3, 0,   28, 8)

```

### G_MOBILS.B: Mobil for the Racing Controller

**File:** `G_MOBILS.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 6,458 bytes, 226 lines. Shown as the differences from `G_MOBIL.B`. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_MOBILS.B",R`.

The same game as `G_MOBIL.B`, changed to read the analogue wheel of the SEGA Racing Controller.

**Techniques:**

- Reading an analogue axis with `PAD(0,3)` (neutral 127) instead of the digital pad
- Waiting for the right controller before starting

```diff
--- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e1b04427-ae14-5219-80c7-9ef182228cfe/scratchpad/build/../cd/G_MOBIL.B
+++ /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e1b04427-ae14-5219-80c7-9ef182228cfe/scratchpad/build/../cd/G_MOBILS.B
@@ -1,5 +1,7 @@
 LOAD "COM:D"
+'MOBIL Racing Controller version
+'X input item number = 3 (Neutral = 127)
 SCREEN 5,4,256:SKCLOSE
 '----------------------------------
-'BGM & sound effects set
+'BGM & sound effects set   by nao-chan
 PLAYINIT "EXTRA4"
@@ -11,2 +13,9 @@
 PRIORITY 4,7
+*KEY_LOOP
+IF PAD(0,0)=19 THEN *START
+LOCATE 6,8: PRINT "    Plug the Racing Controller"
+LOCATE 6,10:PRINT "into control port 1"
+GOTO *KEY_LOOP
+*START
+CLS
 '----------------------------------
@@ -90,5 +99,5 @@
 PVX     = 0           :'Player Y speed
-PVA     = .025        :'Player acceleration parameter
+PVA     = .035        :'Player acceleration parameter
 BRK     = .02         :'Deceleration parameter
-DIR_PRM = .003
+DIR_PRM = 0
 F=0
@@ -120,6 +129,6 @@
 PDL = PAD(0,1)
+S_PDL = (PAD(0,3) -127) /6000
+DIR = DIR +S_PDL
 '
-IF PDL AND @PAD_LEFT  THEN DIR = DIR - DIR_PRM
 IF DIR < 0 THEN DIR = DIR + 1
-IF PDL AND @PAD_RIGHT THEN DIR = DIR + DIR_PRM
 IF DIR > 1 THEN DIR = DIR - 1
@@ -134,4 +143,4 @@
 AY=-PVA*XSIN(DIR)
-IF PDL AND @PAD_R THEN PVX=PVX+AX: PVY=PVY+AY
-IF PDL AND @PAD_L THEN PVX=PVX-AX: PVY=PVY-AY
+IF PDL AND @PAD_DOWN THEN PVX=PVX+AX: PVY=PVY+AY
+IF PDL AND @PAD_UP THEN PVX=PVX-AX: PVY=PVY-AY
 '
```

### G_BOMB.B: Bomb

**File:** `G_BOMB.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 6,573 bytes, 249 lines. 229 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_BOMB.B",R`.

A multi-player bomb game for the Multi-Terminal 6 multitap: up to six players move around and drop bombs (A button) that explode. It needs at least two pads.

**Techniques:**

- Counting connected pads with `PAD(-1)` and refusing to start with fewer than two
- A main loop that is just a list of `GOSUB` calls: move, explode, collision check, game-over check
- Start positions read from `DATA` with `RESTORE`
- 2D sprites placed with `PUTSPRITE`, one per player and one per bomb

```
  100 ' G_Bomb.B
  110 DIM PPOSX(6),PPOSY(6),PSTAT(6),PADNUM(6)
  120 DIM BSTAT(6,10),BCOUNT(6,10)
  130 DIM SPPAT(16,16)
  150 *START
  160 SCREEN 0
  170 IF ( PAD(-1) <2 ) OR (PAD(-1)=255) THEN LOCATE 0,12:PRINT " Plug two or more control pads":print " into the Multi-Terminal 6":print " please":END
  180 LOCATE 5,12
  190 PRINT "Press Start"
  210 *SLOOP
  220 GOSUB *BTNWAIT
  230 IF (TRIG AND @PAD_START)=0 THEN *SLOOP
  240 CLS
  250 SPRWINDOW,,,,,0,0
  260 ' Game Define
  270 COUNTMAX = 15
  280 BSIZE = 64:EXTIME = 2:ERTIME = 16:HOLDTIME = 4
  290 SPEED = 8:PMAX = 6:BOMBMAX = 10
  300 '
  310 GOSUB *SETUP
  330 *MAIN
  340 GOSUB *MOVE
  350 GOSUB *EXPLOSE
  360 GOSUB *COLI_CHECK
  370 GOSUB *CHECK
  380 IF OVER = 1 THEN *GAMEOVER
  390 VSYNC
  400 GOTO *MAIN
  410 '
  420 ' setup
  430 '
  450 *SETUP
  460 ' Data Init
  470 FOR I=0 TO PMAX-1
  480  PADNUM(I)=-1
  490  PPOSX(I)=-1
  500  PPOSY(I)=-1
  510  PSTAT(I)=-1
  520  FOR J=0 TO BOMBMAX-1
  530   BSTAT(I,J)=-1
  540  NEXT J
  550 NEXT I
  560 ' Pad Check
  570 PD = 0
  580 FOR I=0 TO PMAX-1
  590  IF PAD(I,0) = 2 THEN PADNUM(PD)=I:PSTAT(PD)=0:PD = PD+1
  595  dummy=pad(i,2)
  600 NEXT I
  610 PNUM = PD
  620 ' Position Set
  630 GOSUB *INIT_SPR
  640 RESTORE *STARTPOS
  650 FOR I=0 TO PNUM-1
  660  READ PPOSX(I),PPOSY(I)
  670  PUTSPRITE I+1,(PPOSX(I),PPOSY(I)),I+1
  680  OBJ(I+1,@XS)=.5,.5,.5
  690  OBJ(I+1,@GROUP)=1
  700  OBJ(I+1,@RADIUS)=4
  710 NEXT I
  720 '
  730 RETURN
  740 '
  750 ' Move
  760 '
  780 *MOVE
  790 FOR I=0 TO PNUM-1
  800  IF PSTAT(I)=-1 THEN *MSKIP
  810  TRIG = PAD(PADNUM(I),2)
  820  LEVEL= PAD(PADNUM(I),1)
  830  IF LEVEL AND @PAD_LEFT THEN PPOSX(I)=PPOSX(I)-SPEED:IF PPOSX(I)<16 THEN PPOSX(I)=16
  840  IF LEVEL AND @PAD_RIGHT THEN PPOSX(I)=PPOSX(I)+SPEED:IF PPOSX(I)>304 THEN PPOSX(I)=303
  850  IF LEVEL AND @PAD_UP THEN PPOSY(I)=PPOSY(I)-SPEED:IF PPOSY(I)<16 THEN PPOSY(I)=16
  860  IF LEVEL AND @PAD_DOWN THEN PPOSY(I)=PPOSY(I)+SPEED:IF PPOSY(I)>208 THEN PPOSY(I)=207
  870  IF TRIG  AND @PAD_A THEN GOSUB *DROP_BOMB
  890 *MSKIP
  900 NEXT I
  910 GOSUB *SHOW_PLAYER
  920 RETURN
  930 '
  950 *DROP_BOMB
  960  FOR J=0 TO BOMBMAX-1
  970   IF BSTAT(I,J)<>-1 THEN *DNX
  980    BNUM=I*BOMBMAX+J+PMAX+1
  990    BSTAT(I,J)=0
 1000    BCOUNT(I,J)=COUNTMAX
 1010    PUTSPRITE BNUM,(PPOSX(I),PPOSY(I)),0
 1020    OBJ(BNUM,@XS)=.25,.25,.25
 1030    OBJ(BNUM,@RADIUS)=2
 1040    OBJ(BNUM,@GROUP)=2
 1050    GOTO *DSKIP
 1070 *DNX
 1080  NEXT J
 1100 *DSKIP
 1110  RETURN
 1120 '
 1130 ' Explose
 1140 '
 1160 *EXPLOSE
 1170 FOR I=0 TO PNUM-1
 1180  FOR J=0 TO BOMBMAX-1
 1190   STAT = BSTAT(I,J)
 1200   BNUM=I*BOMBMAX+J+PMAX+1
 1210   IF STAT=-1 THEN *ESKIP
 1220   IF STAT>0  THEN *SHOWEXP
 1230   BCOUNT(I,J)=BCOUNT(I,J)-1
 1240   IF BCOUNT(I,J)=0 THEN BSTAT(I,J)=1:OBJ(BNUM,@GROUP)=4:OBJ(BNUM,@RADIUS)=0
 1260 *ESKIP
 1270   NEXT J
 1280 NEXT I
 1290 RETURN
 1300 '
 1320 *SHOWEXP
 1330 SIZE=BCOUNT(I,J)/16
 1340 OBJ(BNUM,@XS)=SIZE,SIZE,SIZE
 1350 OBJ(BNUM,@RADIUS)=BCOUNT(I,J)/2
 1360 IF STAT = 1 THEN BCOUNT(I,J)=BCOUNT(I,J)+(BSIZE/EXTIME):IF BCOUNT(I,J)>=BSIZE THEN BSTAT(I,J)=2+HOLDTIME
 1370 IF STAT = 2 THEN BCOUNT(I,J)=BCOUNT(I,J)-(BSIZE/ERTIME):IF BCOUNT(I,J)<1 THEN BSTAT(I,J)=-1:OBJ(BNUM,@TYPE)=0
```

### G_HATA.B: Hata-age (Flag Up)

**File:** `G_HATA.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 54,007 bytes, 1,281 lines. 600 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_HATA.B",R`.

A one- or two-player reaction game. The referee calls out commands such as "red up, white don't lower" and you must raise or lower the red and white flags correctly in time. Scores, a timer, a sun and clouds are drawn as polygons.

**Techniques:**

- `ON INTERVAL` timer interrupts to read each pad and update the clock 60 times a second, separate from the main loop
- Building the spoken command from subject and predicate word lists in `DATA`
- Two players on one screen, each with its own pad handler
- Polygon objects for the people, the sun and the clouds; BG windows drawn with `LINE`
- `COLOROFS` fades and `EFFECT` sound effects

> The Tutorial Manual's list of supplied programs describes it (TM section 2.10).

### G_MAZE.B: Maze

**File:** `G_MAZE.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 17,901 bytes, 648 lines. 644 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_MAZE.B",R`.

A first-person 3D maze. The maze is generated at random, turned into polygons, and you must find the exit within the time limit. Six one-use items, one per button, help you: a telescope view from above, walking through walls and more.

**Techniques:**

- Random maze generation into a 2D array
- Turning the whole maze into one polygon object, so it needs few objects (see the comment at the top)
- Moving the camera through the maze one cell at a time with smooth turning
- Items placed at random and picked up by position, with a replay that keeps the same layout
- `ON INTERVAL` for the countdown

### G_JUMP.B: Jump

**File:** `G_JUMP.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 126,444 bytes, 3,774 lines. 544 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_JUMP.B",R`.

A 3D game where you steer and jump between floating platforms, with gravity and acceleration, small textured polygon models and its own instrument set for the music.

**Techniques:**

- Physics with speed, acceleration and gravity variables
- Small 8x8 textures (`SETTEX`) and polygon models (`SETVERTEX`/`SETPOLYGON`) read from `DATA`, which is most of the file
- `TARG READ` to build a custom instrument set, `SETSONG` and `BGM` for music
- `ON INTERVAL` clock, and `PALETTE` set-up for a 256-colour texture

### G_JUMP_A.B: Jump for the Multi Controller

**File:** `G_JUMP_A.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 126,751 bytes, 3,789 lines. Shown as the differences from `G_JUMP.B`. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_JUMP_A.B",R`.

`G_JUMP.B` changed to use the analogue stick and triggers of the SEGA Multi Controller (the 3D pad) in analogue mode.

**Techniques:**

- Analogue stick X and Y in `PAD(0,3)` and `PAD(0,4)` (neutral 128)
- Analogue triggers in `PAD(0,5)` and `PAD(0,6)` (0 to 255), used for a variable-strength jump

```diff

@@ -1,3 +1,17 @@
 LOAD "COM:DUMMY"
+'JUMP Multi Controller version
+'X input item number = 3 (Neutral = 128)
+'Y input item number = 4 (Neutral = 128)
+'Analogue R trigger item number = 5 (Max 255)
+'Analogue L trigger item number = 6 (Max 255)
+'
 SCREEN 6,4,256:SKCLOSE
+*KEY_LOOP
+IF PAD(0,0)=22 THEN *START
+LOCATE 6,8: PRINT "    Switch the SEGA Multi Controller"
+LOCATE 6,10:PRINT "   to analogue mode and"
+LOCATE 6,12:PRINT "into control port 1"
+GOTO *KEY_LOOP
+*START
+CLS
 DISPLAY OFF
@@ -363,6 +377,4 @@
 '
-PDL = PAD(0,1)
-'
-IF PDL AND @PAD_LEFT  THEN DIR = DIR - DIR_PRM
-IF PDL AND @PAD_RIGHT THEN DIR = DIR + DIR_PRM
+PDL = (PAD(0,3) -128) /30000
+DIR = DIR + PDL
 IF DIR > 1 THEN DIR = DIR - 1
@@ -373,4 +385,5 @@
 '
-IF PDL AND @PAD_A THEN JSP = JSP +JUMP
-IF PDL AND @PAD_B THEN JSP = JSP +JUMP_H
+JUMP = PAD(0,5) /30000
+'
+JSP = JSP +JUMP
 IF JSP > 1 THEN JSP = 1
@@ -390,6 +403,7 @@
 TIME_S = 1            :' Clock start
+'
+PVA = (PAD(0,4) -128) /10000

 AY=PVA*COSD
-IF PDL AND @PAD_DOWN THEN PVX=PVX-AX: PVY=PVY-AY
-IF PDL AND @PAD_UP   THEN PVX=PVX+AX: PVY=PVY+AY
+PVX=PVX-AX: PVY=PVY-AY
 GOTO *MOVE
@@ -398,4 +412,4 @@
 PVX=0:PVY=0
-IF PDL AND @PAD_DOWN THEN PVX =-SPEED*SIND: PVY=-SPEED*COSD
-IF PDL AND @PAD_UP   THEN PVX = SPEED*SIND: PVY= SPEED*COSD
+SPEED = (PAD(0,4) -128) /1500
+PVX = -SPEED*SIND: PVY= -SPEED*COSD

 '
+'AGL = PAD(0,6)
+'BANK =-.25*(255-agl)/255:EYE = .25*agl/255
+PDL = PAD(0,1)
 IF PDL AND @PAD_X THEN BANK =  -.25:EYE =    0
@@ -443,10 +460,8 @@
```

### G_SABA.B: Saba (Mackerel)

**File:** `G_SABA.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 167,123 bytes, 2,218 lines. 829 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_SABA.B",R`.

A Virtua Gun shooting gallery. Mackerel leap out of the sea and you shoot them before they fall back. Now and then a fish-man, a surfer or a waiter appears instead. There are two modes, aimed shooting and rapid fire, and a sight calibration screen.

**Techniques:**

- Finding which port the Virtua Gun is in, and reading its X/Y position and trigger from `PAD`
- Calibration: averaging three shots at the centre of the screen
- Sprites with several textured attributes, switched to change what a sprite shows
- Hit testing against each object's rectangle, score and hit-mark objects linked as children
- Appearance positions, speeds and probabilities that change with the level
- `GLOAD` for the background picture

**Files it uses:** `SABA_BG.0` (background picture, 256 colours)

```
 2990 SETATR TOKUTENATR+4,1,READ
 3000 SETATR TOKUTENATR+5,1,READ
 3010 SETATR TOKUTENATR+6,1,READ
 3020 SETATR TOKUTENATR+7,1,READ
 3030 SETATR TOKUTENATR+8,1,READ
 3040 SETATR TOKUTENATR+9,1,READ
 3050 FOR I=1 TO 49
 3060  OBJ(I+TOKUTENOBJ,20)=I+TOKUTENOBJ
 3070  OBJ(I+TOKUTENOBJ,17)=0:'Polygon ID=0
 3080  OBJ(I+TOKUTENOBJ,0)=7
 3090 NEXT
 3100 '
 3110 '****************
 3120 ' BG object settings
 3130 '****************
 3140 RESTORE *BGOBJ_ATR
 3150 SETATR BGATR,1,READ :'Attribute settings
 3160 FOR I=0 TO 2
 3170  OBJ(BGOBJ+I,20)=BGOBJ+I:'Hide
 3180  OBJ(BGOBJ+I, 0)=4:'Polygon display
 3190  OBJ(BGOBJ+I,16)=BGATR,0:'
 3200 NEXT
 3210  OBJ(BGOBJ  , 4)=0,100:'Score window
 3220  OBJ(BGOBJ+1, 4)=-145,-115:'Game mode
 3230  OBJ(BGOBJ+2, 4)=125,-115:'Time left, misses
 3240  OBJ(BGOBJ  ,12)=8,1:'Polygon scale: X,Y,Z
 3250  OBJ(BGOBJ+1,12)=2,.35:'Polygon scale: X,Y,Z
 3260  OBJ(BGOBJ+2,12)=3,.35:'Polygon scale: X,Y,Z
 3270 '
 3280 '********************
 3290 ' Set up the title (end title)
 3300 '********************
 3310 RESTORE *TITLE_SPRITE
 3320 SETTEX 30,80,80,256,READ :'Load title texture (SA-)
 3330 SETTEX 31,80,80,256,READ :' ..     (FIN-)
 3340 SETTEX 32,80,80,256,READ :' ..     (-ISH)
 3350 SETVERTEX 1,4,READ,(1,1,1,-40,-40,0):'Set vertices
 3360 SETPOLYGON 1,1,1,READ :'Set polygons
 3370 SETATR TITLEATR  ,1,READ :'Set attribute
 3380 SETATR TITLEATR+1,1,READ
 3390 SETATR TITLEATR+2,1,READ
 3400 FOR I=0 TO 2
 3410  OBJ(TITLEOBJ+I,20)=TITLEOBJ+I:'Hide
 3420  OBJ(TITLEOBJ+I, 0)=4:'Polygon display
 3430  OBJ(TITLEOBJ+I,16)=TITLEATR+I,1
 3440 NEXT
 3450 OBJ(TITLEOBJ  , 4)=0,-72:'Set position
 3460 OBJ(TITLEOBJ+1, 4)=-100,72:'Set position
 3470 OBJ(TITLEOBJ+2, 4)=100,72:'Set position
 3480 '
 3490 '***********
 3500 ' Title
 3510 '***********
 3530 *TITLE_START
 3540 GOSUB *TITLE:'Choose the game mode on the title
 3550 COLOROFS (0,0,0):'Initialise colours
 3560 '
 3570 IF OWARI=1 OR GAME_MODE = 3 THEN *END_TITLE:'Game over
 3580 '
 3590 GOSUB *DROW_BG:'Background display
 3600 DISPLAY ON 1:'Screen display
 3610 '
 3620 IF GAME_MODE=0 THEN
 3630  LOCATE 1,1:PRINT "AIMED SHOOTING!!"
 3640 ELSE
 3650  LOCATE 1,1:PRINT "RAPID FIRE!!"
 3660 ENDIF
 3670 '
 3680 LOCATE 10,5:PRINT "READY....";
 3690 VSYNC 60
 3700 PRINT "GO!!!"
 3710 VSYNC 20
 3720 LOCATE 10,5:PRINT "              "
 3730 '
 3750 *START:'Initial display
 3760 'Initialise game parameters
 3770 FIRE=0:'Shots fired
 3780 AVE=0:'Hit rate
 3790 HITNUM=0:'Hit count
 3800 MISSNUM=0:'Miss count
 3810 BULLET=RELOAD:'Bullets left
 3820 SCORE=0:'Score
 3830 TIME_LEV=0:'Game level
 3840 HIT_LEV=0
 3850 'Set up objects for the total number
 3860 FOR I=1 TO OBJNUM
 3870  PRMT(I, 0)=0:'Not present
 3880  PRMT(I, 1)=XSIZE:'Object X size
 3890  PRMT(I, 2)=YSIZE:'Object Y size
 3900  OBJ(I,20)=I:'Hide object
 3910  OBJ(I, 4)=-1000,-1000
 3920  OBJ(I, 0)=7:'Polygon display
 3930 NEXT
 3940 '
 3950 GOSUB *HASSEI:'Character appears
 3960 '
 3970 FOR I=1 TO OBJNUM
 3980  IF PRMT(I,0)=1 THEN
 3990   OBJ(I,20)=0:'Object display
 4000  ENDIF
 4010 NEXT
 4020 '
 4030 'Timer on
 4040 'IF GAME_MODE=1 THEN
 4050  CLK=0:'Time
 4060  INTERVAL (0) ON,1:'1/60 interrupt
 4070 'ELSE
 4080 ' INTERVAL(0) ON,60:'once per second
 4090 'ENDIF
 4100 '
 4110 GOSUB *LEFT_BULLET:'Bullets-left display
 4120 '
 4130 '****************
 4140 '*   Main routine    *
 4150 '****************
 4170 *MAIN
 4180  IF GAME_MODE=0 THEN
 4190   LOCATE 25,1:PRINT USING "MISS:###",INT(MISSNUM)
 4200  ELSE
 4210   LOCATE 25,1:PRINT USING "Time left:###",60-INT(CLK)
 4220  ENDIF
 4230  GOSUB *PRM_DISP:'Message display
 4240  IF GAME_MODE=1 AND TIMEMAX-INT(CLK)<=0 THEN *ENDING:'End when CLK=TIMEMAX
 4250  IF GAME_MODE=0 AND MISSNUM>=MISSMAX THEN *ENDING:'End after MISSMAX misses
 4260 '
 4270  'Change level (every 10 s, change appearance positions)
 4280  IF INT(CLK)<>0 THEN
 4290   TIME_LVL = CLK/10
 4300  ENDIF
 4310 '
 4320  BGUN=GUNCHECK
 4330  GUNCHECK=PAD(GUNPORT,1):'Get the state
 4340  IF BULLET>0 THEN
 4350   'When there are bullets
 4360   IF GUNCHECK=&H400 AND GUNCHECK<>BGUN THEN
 4370    BULLET=BULLET-1:'Reduce bullet count
 4380    GOSUB *VGUN:'Get VGX,VGY
 4390    IF VGX=(0-CLBX) AND VGY=(0-CLBY) THEN
 4400     GOSUB *SOUTEN:'Reload
 4410     GOSUB *LEFT_BULLET
 4420    ELSE
 4430     GOSUB *REACTION
 4440     GOSUB *HIT:'Use VGX,VGY
 4450     GOSUB *LEFT_BULLET
 4460     FIRE=FIRE+1:'Increment shots fired
 4470    ENDIF
 4480   ENDIF
 4490  ELSE
 4500   'When there are no bullets
 4510   IF GUNCHECK=&H400 AND GUNCHECK<>BGUN THEN
 4520    GOSUB *VGUN:'Get VGX,VGY
 4530    IF VGX=(0-CLBX) AND VGY=(0-CLBY) THEN
 4540     GOSUB *SOUTEN:'Reload
 4550     GOSUB *LEFT_BULLET
 4560    ENDIF
 4570   ENDIF
 4580  ENDIF
 4590 '
 4600  'IF GUNCHECK=&H800 THEN CLS -1:'clear screen
 4610  GOSUB *HASSEI
 4620  GOSUB *KANSI
 4630  OBJ(HITMARK,20)=HITMARK:'Erase hit mark
 4640  OBJ(HITMARK+1,20)=HITMARK+1:'Erase miss mark
 4650 GOTO *MAIN
 4660 '
 4670 '****************
 4680 '*   Subroutines    *
 4690 '****************
 4700 'Watch objects
 4720 *KANSI
 4730  FOR KNSI=1 TO OBJNUM
 4740   IF (PRMT(KNSI,0)=1) AND ((OBJ(KNSI,4)<-160) OR (OBJ(KNSI,5)<-112) OR (160<OBJ(KNSI,4)) OR (112<OBJ(KNSI,5))) THEN
 4750     KESI=KNSI:'Argument
 4760     GOSUB *KESIOBJ
 4770     IF GAME_MODE=0 AND PRMT(KNSI,13)=0 THEN MISSNUM=MISSNUM+1:'Escaped off screen (miss)
 4780   ENDIF
 4790  NEXT
 4800 RETURN
 4810 '
 4820 'Erase object
 4840 *KESIOBJ
 4850     PRMT(KESI,0)=0:'Not present
 4860     OBJ(KESI,4)=-1000,-1000:'To where the Virtua Gun can't reach
 4870     OBJ(KESI,20)=KESI:'Hide object
 4880     OBJ(KESI+TOKUTENOBJ,20)=KESI+TOKUTENOBJ:'Detach the score object
 4890 RETURN
 4900 '
 4910 'Appear?
 4930 *HASSEI
 4940  KAKURITU=HIT_LVL:'Appearance probability follows the level
 4950  FOR HSI=1 TO OBJNUM
 4960   RHS=RND(MOTOKAKURITU-(HIT_LVL*100)):'Appearance probability
 4970   IF PRMT(HSI,0)=0 AND KAKURITU>=RHS THEN
 4980    'COLOR RND(7)+1
 4990    'LOCATE 20,21:PRINT "APPEAR!!"
 5000    'COLOR 7
 5010    GOSUB *PRMSETTEI
 5020    GOSUB *OBJSETTEI
 5030   ENDIF
 5040  NEXT
 5050 RETURN
 5060 '
 5070 'Appearance settings
 5090 *PRMSETTEI
 5100  PRMT(HSI, 0)=1:'Present
 5110 '
 5120  HH=HIT_LVL+2:'Follows the game level
 5130  HSIRN=RND(HH):'How it appears
 5140  IF HSIRN<=3 THEN
 5150   'Fixed appearance
 5160   KTIPLUS=RND(TIME_LVL)+1:'Appearance position (changes with level)
 5170   KITEI=KITEI+KTIPLUS:IF KITEI>SHUTUGEN THEN KITEI=KITEI-SHUTUGEN
 5180   HSIICHI=KITEI:'Set appearance position
 5190   PRMT(HSI, 3)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI, 3):'X coordinate
 5200   PRMT(HSI, 4)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI, 4):'Y coordinate
 5210   PRMT(HSI, 5)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI, 5):'X initial speed
 5220   PRMT(HSI, 6)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI, 6):'Y initial speed
 5230   PRMT(HSI, 7)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI, 7):'X acceleration
 5240   PRMT(HSI, 8)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI, 8):'Y acceleration
 5250   PRMT(HSI, 9)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI, 9):'X limiter
 5260   PRMT(HSI,10)=DMYPRMT(HSIICHI,10):'Y limiter
 5270  ELSE
 5280   'Random appearance
 5290   PRMT(HSI, 3)=RND(320)-160:'X coordinate
 5300   PRMT(HSI, 4)=RND(224)-112:'Y coordinate
 5310   PRMT(HSI, 5)=RND(5)+1:'X initial speed
 5320   IF PRMT(HSI,3)>0 THEN PRMT(HSI,5)=-PRMT(HSI,5)
 5330   PRMT(HSI, 6)=-(RND(5)+1):'Y initial speed
 5340   IF PRMT(HSI,4)<-80 THEN PRMT(HSI,5)=0
 5350   PRMT(HSI, 7)=  0:'X acceleration
 5360   PRMT(HSI, 8)=.1:'Y acceleration
 5370   PRMT(HSI, 9)=  5:'X limiter
 5380   PRMT(HSI,10)=  5:'Y limiter
 5390  ENDIF
 5400 '
 5410  'Attribute ID
 5420  IF PRMT(HSI, 5)>0 THEN
 5430    PRMT(HSI,11)=0
 5440   ELSE
 5450    PRMT(HSI,11)=1
 5460  ENDIF
 5470  HITO=RND(100)
 5480  '1 in 100 becomes a fish-man
 5490  IF HITO=0 THEN
 5500   PRMT(HSI,11)=PRMT(HSI,11)+HSABA:'Change attribute from mackerel to fish-man
 5510  ENDIF
 5520  '1 in 100 becomes a surfer
 5530  IF HITO=1 THEN
 5540   PRMT(HSI,11)=PRMT(HSI,11)+SURF:'Change attribute from mackerel to surfer
 5550  ENDIF
 5560  '1 in 100 becomes a waiter
 5570  IF HITO=2 THEN
 5580   PRMT(HSI,11)=PRMT(HSI,11)+SERV:'Change attribute from mackerel to waiter
 5590  ENDIF
 5600  PRMT(HSI,12)=  0:'Polygon ID
 5610  PRMT(HSI,13)=  0:'Hit count
 5620 RETURN
 5630 '
 5640 'Set the object that appears
 5660 *OBJSETTEI
 5670   OBJ(HSI,20)=0:'Object display
 5680   OBJ(HSI,16)=PRMT(HSI,11),PRMT(HSI,12):'Attribute ID=0, polygon ID=0
 5690   OBJ(HSI, 4)=PRMT(HSI,3),PRMT(HSI,4):'X,Y
 5700   OBJ(HSI,24)=PRMT(HSI,5),PRMT(HSI,6):'VX,VY
 5710   OBJ(HSI,28)=PRMT(HSI,7),PRMT(HSI,8):'AX,AY
 5720   OBJ(HSI,33)=PRMT(HSI,9),PRMT(HSI,10):'LX,LY
 5730 RETURN
 5740 '
 5760 *HIT
 5770  FOR HITI=1 TO OBJNUM
 5780   HITX=PRMT(HITI,1)/2:'Hit test X
 5790   HITY=PRMT(HITI,2)/2:'Hit test Y
 5800   MINX=OBJ(HITI,4)-HITX+REVX:'Left edge of the object
 5810   MAXX=OBJ(HITI,4)+HITX+REVX:' Right edge
 5820   MINY=OBJ(HITI,5)-HITY+REVY:'Top edge of the object
 5830   MAXY=OBJ(HITI,5)+HITY+REVY:' Bottom edge
 5840   IF (TRG=1) AND MINX<=VGX AND VGX<=MAXX AND MINY<=VGY AND VGY<=MAXY THEN
 5850    IF PRMT(HITI,13)=0 THEN OBJ(HITI,16)=OBJ(HITI,16)+HANTEN:'First hit: upside down
 5860    PRMT(HITI,13)=PRMT(HITI,13)+1:'Increment hit count
 5870    GOSUB *KODOMO:'Attach the score object
 5880    SCORE=SCORE+PRMT(HITI,13)*100
 5890    IF 0<=PRMT(HITI,13) AND PRMT(HITI,13)<=9 THEN
 5900     'Falls away
 5910     OBJ(HITI,24)=0,0:'VX,VY
 5920     OBJ(HITI,28)=0,.1:'AX,AY
 5930    ENDIF
 5940    IF HITMAX<=PRMT(HITI,13) THEN
 5950     'Hit-count upper limit
 5960     KESI=HITI:'Argument for KESIOBJ
 5970     GOSUB *KESIOBJ:'Erase object
 5980    ENDIF
 5990    OBJ(HITMARK, 4)=VGX-REVX,VGY-REVY:'Move the hit-mark object
 6000    OBJ(HITMARK,20)=0:'Show the hit mark
 6010    VSYNC 1:'Wait for display
 6020    TRG=0:'Virtua Gun trigger off
 6030    HITNUM=HITNUM+1:'Increment hit count
 6040    'Hit level (changes number appearing)
 6050    HIT_LVL=INT(HITNUM/10)
 6060   ENDIF
 6070  NEXT
 6080  IF TRG=1 THEN
 6090   OBJ(HITMARK+1, 4)=VGX-REVX,VGY-REVY:'Move the miss-mark object
 6100   OBJ(HITMARK+1,20)=0:'Show the miss mark
 6110   VSYNC 3
 6120   MISSNUM=MISSNUM+1:'Increment miss count
 6130  ENDIF
 6140  TRG=0:'Trigger off on a miss
 6150 RETURN
 6160 '
 6170 '*******************
 6180 ' Attach the score object
 6190 '*******************
 6210 *KODOMO
 6220  OBJ(HITI+TOKUTENOBJ,20)=HITI:'Attach to the parent object
 6230  OBJ(HITI+TOKUTENOBJ, 4)=10
 6240  OBJ(HITI+TOKUTENOBJ, 5)=-10
 6250  OBJ(HITI+TOKUTENOBJ, 6)=-10
 6260  OBJ(HITI+TOKUTENOBJ,16)=PRMT(HITI,13)+TOKUTENATR-1:'Set score attribute
 6270 RETURN
 6280 '
 6290 '************
 6300 'Parameter display
 6310 '************
 6330 *PRM_DISP
 6340  LOCATE 2,22:PRINT USING "Score     =########";SCORE
 6350  'LOCATE 2,23:PRINT USING "Bullets left=  ##";BULLET
 6360 RETURN
 6370 '
 6380 '************
 6390 'Time
 6400 '************
 6420 *CLK_UP
 6430   CLK=CLK+.0167:'Time increases
 6440 RETURN
 6450 '
 6460 '************
 6470 'End
 6480 '************
 6500 *ENDING
 6510  INTERVAL (0) OFF :'Stop interrupts
 6520  CLS :GOSUB *NOT_OBJDISP:'Hide object
 6530  OBJ(BGOBJ  , 4)=0,-30:'Score window
 6540  OBJ(BGOBJ  ,12)=4.5,3:'Polygon scale: X,Y,Z
 6550  OBJ(BGOBJ  ,20)=0:'Display
 6560  LOCATE END_X+3,END_Y:PRINT "FINISHED!!!"
 6570  LOCATE END_X,END_Y+2:PRINT "Score     :";SCORE
 6580  IF GAME_MODE=0 THEN
 6590   IF FIRE<>0 THEN
 6600    AVE=HITNUM/FIRE
 6610   ELSE
 6620    AVE=0
 6630   ENDIF
 6640   LOCATE END_X,END_Y+1:PRINT "Game mode: AIMED SHOOTING"
 6650   LOCATE END_X,END_Y+3:PRINT USING "Hit rate   :###.##%";AVE*100
 6660   LOCATE END_X,END_Y+4:PRINT "Shots fired :";FIRE
 6670   LOCATE END_X,END_Y+5:PRINT "Misses     :";MISSNUM
 6680  ELSE
 6690   LOCATE END_X,END_Y+1:PRINT "Game mode: RAPID FIRE"
 6700  ENDIF
 6710  COLOR (2)
 6720  LOCATE END_X,END_Y+8:PRINT "PRESS START BUTTON"
 6730  COLOR (7)
 6750 *END_GUN_LOOP
 6760  GUNCHECK=PAD(GUNPORT,1):'Get the state
 6770  IF GUNCHECK<>&H800 THEN *END_GUN_LOOP:'Stop until START is pressed
 6780  GOSUB *BLACKOUT
 6790  OBJ(BGOBJ  , 4)=0,100:'Restore the score window
 6800  OBJ(BGOBJ  ,12)=8,.8:'Polygon scale: X,Y,Z
 6810  OBJ(BGOBJ  ,20)=BGOBJ:'Hide
 6820  DISPLAY OFF 1
 6830  CLS :'Clear the screen
 6840 GOTO *TITLE_START

21150 '
21160 '*****************
21170 'Get Virtua Gun XY
21180 '-----------------
21190 ' VGX: X coordinate
21200 ' VGY: Y coordinate
21210 ' GUNPORT: port the Virtua Gun is plugged into
21220 ' TRG: trigger flag
21230 ' CLBX: calibration X
21240 ' CLBY:          Y
21250 ' DEVICE ID = 37(&H25)
21260 ' Trigger=&H400
21270 ' Start=&H800
21280 ' Merge=&HC00
21290 '*****************
21310 *VGUN
21320  COLOROFS (FLSHRED,FLSHBLU,FLSHGRN):'Flash
21330  COLOR,,,FLSHBG:'BG flash
21340  VSYNC 5:'Wait to read coordinates
21350  VGX=(PAD(GUNPORT,3)/2)-CLBX:'Adjust coordinate X
21360  VGY=PAD(GUNPORT,4)-CLBY:'Adjust coordinate Y
21370  COLOROFS (OFSRED,OFSBLU,OFSGRN):'Restore
21380  COLOR,,,BGCLR:'Restore BG
21390  'VGX=((PAD(GUNPORT,3)-90)*(320/650))-CLBX:'adjust coordinates?
21400 RETURN
21410 '
21420 '****************
21430 ' Correct coordinate position
21440 '----------------
21450 'CLBX: Virtua Gun correction X
21460 'CLBY: Virtua Gun correction Y
21470 'REVX: X correction value
21480 'REVY: Y correction value
21490 'DIM TEMPCLBX(3),TEMPCLBY(3):'temporary for correction
21500 'CLBX=0:CLBY=0:'calibration
21510 '****************
21530 *CALIBRATE
21540  ACTIVE 0:'Draw on screen 0
21550  CLBX=0:CLBY=0:'Calibration
21560  REVX=160:REVY=112
21570  TEMPCLBX(0)=0
21580  TEMPCLBY(0)=0
21590  CLS 0:CLS :'Clear the screen
21600  COLOR (7)
21610  LINE (0,0)-(319,223),7,BF
21620  LINE (10,198)-(309,214),A,BF
21630  CIRCLE (160,112),10,1,F
21640  CIRCLE (160,112),20,1
21650  CIRCLE (160,112),30,1
21660  CIRCLE (160,112),40,1
21670 '
21680  GOSUB *FADEIN:'Fade in
21690 '
21700  LOCATE 10,24:PRINT "Shoot the centre of the screen!!! (3 times)"
21710  CLBRT=1
21730 *CLBGUN:BGUN=GUNCHECK:GUNCHECK=PAD(GUNPORT,1):'Get the state
21740   IF GUNCHECK=&H400 AND BGUN<>&H400 THEN
21750    GOSUB *VGUN:'Get VGX,VGY
21760   ELSE
21770    GOTO *CLBGUN:'Go back if not shot
21780   ENDIF
21790   'LOCATE 1,10+CLBRT:PRINT USING "# shot:X:### Y:###";CLBRT;VGX;VGY
21800   'CIRCLE(VGX,VGY),1,0,F:'show provisional hit mark
21810   TEMPCLBX(CLBRT)=VGX
21820   TEMPCLBY(CLBRT)=VGY
21830   CLBRT=CLBRT+1
21840  IF CLBRT<=3 THEN GOTO *CLBGUN:'Go back until 3 shots
21850  FOR CLBI=1 TO 3
21860   TEMPCLBX(0)=TEMPCLBX(0)+TEMPCLBX(CLBI):'X total
21870   TEMPCLBY(0)=TEMPCLBY(0)+TEMPCLBY(CLBI):'Y
21880  NEXT
21890  CLBX=TEMPCLBX(0)/3-REVX:'X correction
21900  CLBY=TEMPCLBY(0)/3-REVY:'Y correction
21910  CLS
21920  LOCATE 9,24:PRINT "Press START to return to the title"
21940 *CLBGUNLOOP
21950  BGUN=GUNCHECK:GUNCHECK=PAD(GUNPORT,1):'Get the state
21960  IF GUNCHECK=&H400 AND BGUN<>&H400 THEN
21970   GOSUB *VGUN:'Get VGX,VGY
21980   CIRCLE (VGX,VGY),1,0,F:'Show provisional hit mark
21990  ENDIF
22000  IF GUNCHECK <> &H800 THEN *CLBGUNLOOP
22010  GOSUB *BLACKOUT
22020  CLS 0:CLS
22030 RETURN
22040 '
22060 *REACTION
22070  EFFECT -1,"@12C":'Gunshot
22080  'CIRCLE(VGX,VGY),5,2,F:'HIT coordinate test
22090  'LOCATE 10,4:PRINT USING "SHOTX=### SHOTY=###";VGX;VGY
22100  TRG=1:'Trigger flag ON
22110 RETURN
22120 '
22140 *SOUTEN
22150  BEEP :'Reload on
22160  BULLET=RELOAD:'Load the gun
22170 RETURN
22180 '
22200 *TITLE
22210  GOSUB *FADEIN
22220  TITLE_X=10:TITLE_Y=10
22230  CLS :'Clear the screen
22240  COLOR 7
22250  'LOCATE 15,10:PRINT "MACKEREL!!!!!"
22260  OBJ(TITLEOBJ,20)=0:'Display
22270  VSYNC 60
22280   LOCATE TITLE_X+3,TITLE_Y+2:PRINT "AIMED SHOOTING"
22290   LOCATE TITLE_X+3,TITLE_Y+3:PRINT "RAPID FIRE"
22300   LOCATE TITLE_X+3,TITLE_Y+4:PRINT "CALIBRATE SIGHTS"
22310   LOCATE TITLE_X+3,TITLE_Y+5:PRINT "Game over"
22330 *TITLE_LOOP
22340   GUNCHECK=PAD(GUNPORT,1):'Get the state
22350   IF GUNCHECK=&H400 THEN GAME_MODE=GAME_MODE+1:IF GAME_MODE>=4 THEN GAME_MODE=0
22360   IF GUNCHECK=&H800 THEN *TITLE_LOOP_END
22370   IF GUNCHECK=&HC000 THEN OWARI=1:GOTO *TITLE_LOOP_END:'Game over
```

### G_THESEU.B: Theseus

**File:** `G_THESEU.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 40,400 bytes, 1,232 lines. 900 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_THESEU.B",R`.

A maze action game with ten stages. You guide the hero through each maze, collecting items and avoiding enemies. Each stage's maze, items, enemies and settings are separate data files on the CD.

**Techniques:**

- Loading level data from CD files with `OPEN` and `FREAD`
- Character (tile) graphics for walls, player, enemies and items, set up from data files
- A level loop: initialise, read items and enemies, draw, play, then go to the next level or back to the title
- `ON TIMER` to count frames, `SCROLL` for the screen
- Many small subroutines (over 60 `GOSUB` targets): a good example of breaking a big program up

**Files it uses:** `PALWIN.D`, `BGCHR.D`, `WLCHR.D`, `MYCHR.D`, `ENECHR.D`, `YAKCHR.D`, `HEROCHR.D` (palette and character data); `MAZE01.D`-`MAZE10.D`, `ITEM01.D`-`ITEM10.D`, `ENEM01.D`-`ENEM10.D`, `INID01.D`-`INID10.D` (per-stage data)

### G_TEKE.B: Teke-teke

**File:** `G_TEKE.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 205,646 bytes, 4,491 lines. 2,223 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_TEKE.B",R`.

A virtual-pet and ball game. Three creatures, Pokepoke, Pikepike and Pekepeke, live in a small world. You feed them, make them study and play a ball game against them. Their life, motivation, experience, hunger, sleepiness and mood change over time, and they can die and come back. Progress can be saved to cartridge RAM.

**Techniques:**

- A large state machine with many parameters per character
- Shuttle Mouse or control pad, detected at start
- Saving and loading the game with `OPEN`, `FWRITE` and `FREAD`, with error handling
- Icons, a toolbar and parameter windows drawn with objects and `LINE`
- `COLOROFS` and `MOSAIC` effects, `GLOAD` pictures for the opening and ending

**Files it uses:** `TEKST.1`, `TEKEND.1` (opening and ending pictures, 32768 colours)

> At about 2,200 lines of code this is the biggest game on the CD.

### G_BOU.B: Bou (Stick): starter

**File:** `G_BOU.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 109 bytes, 6 lines. Run it with `LOAD "CD:G_BOU.B",R`.

A six-line program that shows a loading message and runs `BOU_SCD.B`. The game is split over three files because it is too big to load at once.

**Techniques:**

- Chaining programs with `LOAD "CD:name",R`

```
1 '1998/3/19
2 SKCLOSE
3 SCREEN 1
4 LOCATE 12,15:PRINT "NOW LOADING...."
5 LOAD "CD:BOU_SCD.B",R
6 END
```

### BOU_SCD.B: Bou: opening

**File:** `BOU_SCD.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 197,870 bytes, 2,900 lines. 266 lines shown.

The first part of "Bou": checks for a Virtua Gun or Shuttle Mouse, then plays the opening, a camera fly-through of textured polygon objects, before running `BOU_TCD.B`.

**Techniques:**

- Moving the camera smoothly from one point to another in steps
- Building textured objects from vertex, face and texture data in `DATA`
- Detecting the input device

```
  100 '--------------------------------------
  110 '  BOU 1.03  OPENING
  120 '
  130 '  Programed by Script Arts.Co.,Ltd.

  197 GOTO *P_LOOP

  390     CC_Y=CC_Y-C_Y/10000
  430   XXX=XXX+DXX
  431   YYY=YYY+DYY

  450       IF ABS(CC_X)<.01 THEN GOTO *OP_END2
  460 NEXT
  480 *OP_END2
  490 VSYNC 120
  500 FOR N=0 TO 5100
  510    CAMERA (XSIN(N/10000)*XCOS(N/10000)*300,XSIN(N/10000)*XSIN(N/10000)*300,C_Z-N/10) TO (0,0,0)

  570    ENDIF
```

### BOU_TCD.B: Bou: texture and object set-up

**File:** `BOU_TCD.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 136,175 bytes, 2,256 lines. 124 lines shown.

The second part of "Bou": loads the textures, sets up the BG and registers all the objects, then runs `BOU_MCD.B`.

**Techniques:**

- Registering many textures and objects from `DATA`, then handing over to the next program

### BOU_MCD.B: Bou: main program

**File:** `BOU_MCD.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 38,422 bytes, 1,031 lines. 987 lines shown.

The game itself. You ride a vehicle along a course; aliens swing their arms and you must avoid being hit, while animals (a monkey, a panda, a gorilla) move about and tiles appear. Works with a Virtua Gun, Shuttle Mouse or control pad.

**Techniques:**

- A main loop of `GOSUB` calls with an `ON INTERVAL` pad handler
- Hit tests based on distance from a rotating arm
- Object animation for many moving parts (over 270 `OBJ` references)
- A time bar and window drawn with `LINE`

```

 2870   ENDIF
 2880  ENDIF
 2890 '
 2900  A=XTAN(OBJ(OBJ_NOM+3,10)):B=B8_Y1-A*B8_X1
 2910  IF ABS(A)>.0001 THEN
 2920   IF (PY>B8_Y1 AND B8_Y2>B8_Y1) OR (PY<=B8_Y1 AND B8_Y2<=B8_Y1) THEN
 2930    IF (PX<B8_X1 AND B8_X2<B8_X1) OR (PX>=B8_X1 AND B8_X2>=B8_X1) THEN
 2940    IF ((PX-B8_X1)^2+(PY-B8_Y1)^2)<256*OBJ(OBJ_NOM+3,12)^2 THEN :'Whether inside the arm's radius
 2950    OBJX1=(PY+PX/A-B)/(A+1/A)
 2960    OBJY1=A*OBJX1+B
 2970     IF (OBJY1-PY)^2+(OBJX1-PX)^2<64 THEN
 2980       CB$="(B<C<G)":B$="(DFA>E)":EFFECT -1,"@24"+CB$
 2990       HIT_P=HIT_P+1
 3000     ENDIF
 3010     ENDIF
 3020    ENDIF
 3030   ENDIF
 3040  ENDIF

 3080    IF ABS(PX-B7_X1)<14 AND ABS(PY-B7_Y1)<14 THEN

 3110    ENDIF
 3120   ENDIF

 3140    IF ABS(PX-B9_X1)<14 AND ABS(PY-B9_Y1)<14 THEN
 3150     CB$="(B<C<G)":B$="(DFA>E)":EFFECT -1,"@5"+CB$

 3210   ENDIF

 3590  HIT_PP=HIT_P

 3650   IF HITPOI=0 AND P<>1024 AND ((CHRPAT>=40 AND CHRPAT<=46) OR CHRPAT>=56) AND HIT_TIMER>5 THEN
 3660           CB$="(B<C<G)":B$="(DFA>E)":EFFECT -1,"@4"+CB$

 3800 *MOVE_OBJ
 3810 '***********START AND END
 3820    OBJ(180,4)=OBJXY(180,4)-SCROLL_X
 3830    OBJ(181,4)=OBJXY(181,4)-SCROLL_X
 3840 '***********Both hands moving up and down
 3850    FOR RK=0 TO 9
 3860     IF OBJ(140+RK,20)=0 THEN
 3870 '      OBJ(140+RK,5)=OBJXY(140+RK,5)+XCOS(K0*(RK+1))*(64-2*RK)
 3880        OBJ(140+RK,25)=XCOS(K0+1)
 3890        IF K0>999 THEN K0=0 ELSE K0=K0+.008
 3900     ENDIF
 3910       OBJ(140+RK,4)=OBJXY(140+RK,4)-SCROLL_X
 3920    NEXT
 3930 '************Arm movement: rotation
 3940    FOR OBJ_NOM=100 TO 135 STEP 5
 3950      IF OBJ(OBJ_NOM,20)=0 THEN
 3960          OBJ(OBJ_NOM,4)=OBJXY(OBJ_NOM,4)-SCROLL_X
 3970 '         FOR J=OBJ_NOM+1 TO OBJ_NOM+4:OBJ(J,10)=XSIN(K1/J):NEXT
 3980 '         IF K1>999 THEN K1=0 ELSE K1=K1+.05
 3990      ENDIF
 4000    NEXT
 4010 '************Tiles appear
 4020    FOR RK=0 TO 69
 4030      IF OBJ(10+RK,20)=0 AND ABS(PX-OBJ(10+RK,4))<320 THEN
 4040         TI_SIZE=ABS(XCOS(K2*(RK+1))+1)
 4050         IF TI_SIZE>1 THEN TI_SIZE=1
 4060         OBJ(10+RK,12)=TI_SIZE,TI_SIZE
 4070      ENDIF
 4080         OBJ(10+RK,4)=OBJXY(10+RK,4)-SCROLL_X
 4090 '    IF K2>999 THEN K2=0 ELSE K2=K2+.001
 4100    NEXT
 4110         IF K2>999 THEN K2=0 ELSE K2=K2+.005
 4120 '************Animal movement
 4130 DOUXY=MAP_NO
 4140   FOR RK=0 TO 29
 4150     IF OBJ(150+RK,20)=0 THEN
 4160      DOX=INT((OBJ(150+RK,4)+160+SCROLL_X)/8)
 4170      DOY=INT((OBJ(150+RK,5)+112)/8)
 4180        DOUBG=GETCHR(5,(DOX,DOY))/2
 4190 '::::::::::::::::
 4200 ':OBJXY(?,6)= DY:
 4210 ':OBJXY(?,7)= DX:
 4220 '::::::::::::::::
 4230 'Move vertically
 4240        IF DOUBG>=28 AND DOUBG<=31 THEN
 4250           IF OBJXY(150+RK,6)=0 THEN OBJXY(150+RK,6)=DOUXY
 4260             OBJXY(150+RK,7)=0
 4270             OBJXY(150+RK,8)=0
 4280        ELSE
 4290           IF OBJXY(150+RK,3)>=28 AND OBJXY(150+RK,3)<=31 AND DOUBG<28 THEN
 4300              OBJXY(150+RK,6)=-OBJXY(150+RK,6)
 4310              OBJXY(150+RK,8)=0
 4320           ENDIF
 4330        ENDIF
 4340 'Move horizontally
 4350        IF DOUBG>=32 AND DOUBG<=35 THEN
 4360           IF OBJXY(150+RK,7)=0 THEN OBJXY(150+RK,7)=DOUXY
 4370             OBJXY(150+RK,6)=0
 4380             OBJXY(150+RK,8)=0
 4390        ELSE
 4400           IF OBJXY(150+RK,3)>=32 AND OBJXY(150+RK,3)<=35 AND DOUBG<28 THEN
 4410              OBJXY(150+RK,7)=-OBJXY(150+RK,7)
 4420              OBJXY(150+RK,8)=0
 4430           ENDIF
 4440        ENDIF
 4450 'Change direction
 4460        IF DOUBG>=36 AND DOUBG<=39 THEN
 4470          DOUBG1=36
 4480      '    IF ((OBJXY(150+RK,3)=DOUBG1 OR OBJXY(150+RK,3)=(DOUBG1+2)) AND (DOUBG=(DOUBG1+1) OR DOUBG=(DOUBG1+3))) OR ((OBJXY(150+RK,3)=(DOUBG1+1) OR OBJXY(150+RK,3)=(DOUBG1+3)) AND (DOUBG=(DOUBG1+2) OR DOUBG=DOUBG1)) THEN
 4490      '      OBJXY(150+RK,8)=0
 4500      '    ENDIF
 4510      '    IF ((OBJXY(150+RK,3)=DOUBG1 OR OBJXY(150+RK,3)=(DOUBG1+1)) AND (DOUBG=(DOUBG1+2) OR DOUBG=(DOUBG1+3))) OR ((OBJXY(150+RK,3)=(DOUBG1+2) OR OBJXY(150+RK,3)=(DOUBG1+3)) AND (DOUBG=(DOUBG1+1) OR DOUBG=DOUBG1)) THEN
 4520      '      OBJXY(150+RK,8)=0
 4530      '    ENDIF
 4540          IF OBJXY(150+RK,6)<>0 AND OBJXY(150+RK,8)<>1 THEN
 4550             DO_Y(150+RK)=DO_Y(150+RK)+OBJXY(150+RK,6)*6
 4560             IF GETCHR(5,(DOX-2,DOY))>=64 AND GETCHR(5,(DOX-2,DOY))<=70 THEN
 4570               OBJXY(150+RK,6)=0:OBJXY(150+RK,7)=-ABS(DOUXY)
 4580             ENDIF
 4590             IF GETCHR(5,(DOX+2,DOY))>=64 AND GETCHR(5,(DOX+2,DOY))<=70 THEN
 4600                OBJXY(150+RK,6)=0:OBJXY(150+RK,7)=ABS(DOUXY)
 4610             ENDIF
 4620             OBJXY(150+RK,8)=1:GOTO *OBJ_FM2
 4630          ELSE
 4640           IF OBJXY(150+RK,7)<>0 AND OBJXY(150+RK,8)<>1 THEN
 4650             DO_X(150+RK)=DO_X(150+RK)+OBJXY(150+RK,7)*6
 4660             IF GETCHR(5,(DOX,DOY-2))>=56 AND GETCHR(5,(DOX,DOY-2))<=62 THEN
 4670               OBJXY(150+RK,6)=-ABS(DOUXY):OBJXY(150+RK,7)=0
 4680             ENDIF
 4690             IF GETCHR(5,(DOX,DOY+2))>=56 AND GETCHR(5,(DOX,DOY+2))<=62 THEN
 4700               OBJXY(150+RK,6)=ABS(DOUXY):OBJXY(150+RK,7)=0
 4710             ENDIF
 4720             OBJXY(150+RK,8)=1:GOTO *OBJ_FM2
 4730           ENDIF
 4740          ENDIF
 4750        ENDIF
 4760 '
 4770       DO_Y(150+RK)=DO_Y(150+RK)+OBJXY(150+RK,6)*1.5
 4780       DO_X(150+RK)=DO_X(150+RK)+OBJXY(150+RK,7)*1.5
 4800 *OBJ_FM2
 4810       OBJ(150+RK,4)=OBJXY(150+RK,4)-SCROLL_X+DO_X(150+RK)
 4820       OBJ(150+RK,5)=OBJXY(150+RK,5)-SCROLL_Y+DO_Y(150+RK)
 4830      OBJXY(150+RK,3)=DOUBG
 4840 '
 4850     ENDIF
 4860   NEXT
 4870 '
 4880 '
 4890 RETURN

 5600 *SUB_MAPSET
 5610 '
 5620  CHRDX=16:CHRDY=16
 5630  KAO_NO=0
 5640  KAO_NO1=0
 5650  KAO_NO2=0
 5660  KAO_NO3=0
 5670  KAO_NO4=1
 5680  FGK1=0:FGK2=0:MAP_Y=0
 5690  FOR N=1 TO MAP_NO
 5700   MAP_Y=MAP_Y+MAX_Y(N)
 5710  NEXT
 5720   FOR Y=0 TO MAX_Y(MAP_NO)-1
 5730    FOR X=0 TO 63
 5740      AC$=MID$(A$(Y+MAP_Y-MAX_Y(MAP_NO)),X+1,1)
 5750      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=0 THEN CHA=20
 5760      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=1 THEN CHA=12
 5770      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=2 THEN CHA=4
 5780      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=3 THEN CHA=8
 5790      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=4 THEN CHA=16
 5800      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=5 THEN CHA=24
 5810      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=6 THEN :'Animals up/down
 5820        CHA=28
 5830        OBJ(150+KAO_NO2,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX,Y*16-8-112+CHRDY,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0
 5840        OBJXY(150+KAO_NO2,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX
 5850        OBJXY(150+KAO_NO2,5)=Y*16-8-112+CHRDY
 5860        KAO_NO2=KAO_NO2+1
 5870      ENDIF
 5880      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=7 THEN :'Arm-stretching alien
 5890        CHA=20
 5900        OBJ(100+KAO_NO,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX,Y*16-8-112+CHRDY,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0
 5910        OBJXY(100+KAO_NO,4)=OBJ(100+KAO_NO,4)
 5920        KAO_NO=KAO_NO+5
 5930      ENDIF
 5940      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=8 THEN :'Hand-spinning alien
 5950        CHA=20
 5960        OBJ(140+KAO_NO1,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX,Y*16-8-112+CHRDY,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0
 5970        OBJXY(140+KAO_NO1,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX
 5980        OBJXY(140+KAO_NO1,5)=Y*16-8-112+CHRDY
 5990        KAO_NO1=KAO_NO1+1
 6000      ENDIF
 6010      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=9 THEN CHA=28:'Animal moves up/down
 6020      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=10 THEN CHA=32:'Animal moves left/right
 6030      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=11 THEN CHA=36:'Animal changes direction
 6040      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=12 THEN :'Animal moves left/right
 6050        CHA=32
 6060        OBJ(150+KAO_NO2,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX,Y*16-8-112+CHRDY,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0
 6070        OBJXY(150+KAO_NO2,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX
 6080        OBJXY(150+KAO_NO2,5)=Y*16-8-112+CHRDY
 6090        KAO_NO2=KAO_NO2+1
 6100      ENDIF
 6110      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=13 THEN :'Floating/sinking island 1
 6120        CHA=20
 6130        OBJ(10+KAO_NO3,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX,Y*16-8-112+CHRDY,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0
 6140        OBJXY(10+KAO_NO3,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX
 6150        OBJXY(10+KAO_NO3,5)=Y*16-8-112+CHRDY
 6160        KAO_NO3=KAO_NO3+1
 6170      ENDIF
 6180      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=14 THEN :'START button
 6190        CHA=24
 6200        OBJXY(180,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX
 6210        OBJ(180,4)=OBJXY(180,4),Y*16-8-112+CHRDY
 6220        OBJ(180,20)=0
 6230      ENDIF
 6240      IF VAL("&H"+AC$)=15 THEN :'END button
 6250        CHA=24
 6260        OBJXY(181,4)=X*16-8-160+CHRDX
 6270        OBJ(181,4)=OBJXY(181,4),Y*16-8-112+CHRDY
 6280        OBJ(181,20)=0
 6290      ENDIF
 6300      PUTCHR 5,(X*2,Y*2),(CHA)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2+1,Y*2),(CHA+1)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2,Y*2+1),(CHA+2)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2+1,Y*2+1),(CHA+3)*2
 6310    NEXT
 6320   NEXT
 6330 RETURN

 6650     FOR B_ED=75 TO 78:OBJ(B_ED,20)=0:NEXT
 6660     OBJ(10,20)=79:OBJ(20,20)=79:OBJ(10,4)=16,16,,,,,,,1,1:OBJ(20,4)=48,16,,,,,,,1,1
 6670     B_NOB=70:OBJ(B_NOB,4)=64,16:OBJ(B_NOB,20)=79
 6680     EDIT_FG=2:ED_OBJ=1:ED_OBJ2=0:ED_OBJ3=0:ED_OBJ4=0
 6690     FOR X=0 TO 63:FOR Y=0 TO 30:CHA=20:PUTCHR 5,(X*2,Y*2),(CHA)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2+1,Y*2),(CHA+1)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2,Y*2+1),(CHA+2)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2+1,Y*2+1),(CHA+3)*2:NEXT :NEXT
 6700   ENDIF

 6750 *ED_PUT
 6760   IF P=1024 THEN
 6770     X=INT((PX+160+SCROLL_X-4)/16)*2:Y=INT((PY+160+SCROLL_Y-4)/16)*2
 6780     IF ED_OBJ=1 THEN CHA=4:'UP
 6790     IF ED_OBJ=2 THEN CHA=8:'DOWN
 6800     IF ED_OBJ=3 THEN CHA=16:'LEFT
 6810     IF ED_OBJ=4 THEN CHA=12:'RIGHT
 6820     IF ED_OBJ=5 THEN OBJ(11,20)=0:OBJ(11,4)=INT(PX),INT(PY):ED_START=1
 6830     IF ED_OBJ=6 THEN OBJ(21,20)=0:OBJ(21,4)=INT(PX),INT(PY):ED_END=1
 6840     IF ED_OBJ=7 THEN CHA=24:START,END
 6850     IF ED_OBJ=70 THEN OBJ(30+ED_OBJ2,4)=INT(PX),INT(PY):OBJ(30+ED_OBJ2,20)=0:ED_OBJ2=ED_OBJ2+1:IF ED_OBJ2>9 THEN ED_OBJ2=0
 6860     IF ED_OBJ=71 THEN OBJ(30+ED_OBJ2,4)=INT(PX),INT(PY):OBJ(30+ED_OBJ2,20)=0:ED_OBJ2=ED_OBJ2+1:IF ED_OBJ2>9 THEN ED_OBJ2=0
 6870     IF ED_OBJ=72 THEN OBJ(30+ED_OBJ2,4)=INT(PX),INT(PY):OBJ(30+ED_OBJ2,20)=0:ED_OBJ2=ED_OBJ2+1:IF ED_OBJ2>9 THEN ED_OBJ2=0
 6880     IF ED_OBJ=100 THEN OBJ(100+ED_OBJ3,4)=INT(PX),INT(PY):OBJ(100+ED_OBJ3,20)=0:ED_OBJ3=ED_OBJ3+5:IF ED_OBJ3>15 THEN ED_OBJ3=0
 6890     IF ED_OBJ=140 THEN OBJ(140+ED_OBJ4,4)=INT(PX),INT(PY):OBJ(140+ED_OBJ4,20)=0:ED_OBJ4=ED_OBJ4+1:IF ED_OBJ4>9 THEN ED_OBJ4=0
 6900       PUTCHR 5,(X*2,Y*2),(CHA)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2+1,Y*2),(CHA+1)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2,Y*2+1),(CHA+2)*2:PUTCHR 5,(X*2+1,Y*2+1),(CHA+3)*2
```

## 4. Polygon and graphics demos

Short programs that each show one graphics feature, plus the feature demo `DEMO.B`. Most are under 100 lines of code once the model data is left out, so they are easy to study and copy from.

| Program | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`DEMO.B`](#demob-game-basic-feature-demo) | GAME BASIC feature demo |
| [`CLOCK.B`](#clockb-clock) | Clock |
| [`P_CLOCK.B`](#p_clockb-polygon-clock) | Polygon clock |
| [`P_PFONT.B`](#p_pfontb-polygon-font-test-alphabet-soup) | Polygon font test ("Alphabet Soup") |
| [`P_CAME2.B`](#p_came2b-camera-test) | Camera test |
| [`P_SHOWER.B`](#p_showerb-shower) | Shower |
| [`P_TEXMAP.B`](#p_texmapb-texture-drawing-test) | Texture drawing test |
| [`P_FLOWER.B`](#p_flowerb-texture-display-test) | Texture display test |
| [`P_NEKO.B`](#p_nekob-2d-sprite-test) | 2D sprite test |
| [`P_HERI.B`](#p_herib-helicopter-model) | Helicopter model |
| [`P_TANK.B`](#p_tankb-tank-model) | Tank model |
| [`P_DOLL.B`](#p_dollb-doll-animation-editor) | Doll animation editor |
| [`P_DLPLAY.B`](#p_dlplayb-doll-animation-player) | Doll animation player |

### DEMO.B: GAME BASIC feature demo

**File:** `DEMO.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 445,922 bytes, 6,320 lines. 606 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:DEMO.B",R`.

The self-running demo that introduces GAME BASIC's features: graphics commands, polygons, parent-child objects, lights, sprites, texture mapping, BG screens, sound, kanji and the supported peripherals, each with a caption. It runs several of the `P_` demos as parts of itself.

**Techniques:**

- A catalogue of techniques in one program: `PSET`/`LINE`/`CIRCLE`, polygon models, `SETLIGHT`, sprites, textures and `PFONT`
- `KPRINT` captions over the graphics
- Parent-child object trees (the "AZ-1" cube demo)
- `ON INTERVAL` to run animation while the main program shows captions

**Files it uses:** `FONT161.D`, `FONT162.D` (kanji fonts, loaded by `KLOAD`)

```
LOAD"COM:DDD"
 1000 ' GAME BASIC for SEGASATURN Sample Program Ver 1.2
 1001 ' [ DEMO.B ] Feature introduction auto-demo
 1002 ' Programmed by Naozumi Honma (nao)
 1003 '
 1004 '
 1005   SCREEN 0:SKCLOSE:KLOAD ON
 1006   WIDTH 1,1,38,26:COLOR ,RGB(31,31,31)
 1007   PLAYINIT "FH_STAGE",2,50,2,200:RESTORE *MS7:SETSONG
 1008 '----------------------------------
 1009 'Object Item Number
 1010   TYPE = 0: FLAG = 1
 1011   XP = 4: YP = 5: ZP = 6
 1012   XR = 8: YR = 9: ZR = 10
 1013   XS =12: YS =13: ZS = 14
 1014   ATR = 16: POLYGON = 17: ORDER = 18
 1015   PARENT = 20: CHILD = 21
 1016   XV = 24: XA = 28: XL = 32
 1017   XRV = 36: YRV = 37: ZRV = 38
 1018   X0 = 48: Y0 = 49
 1019 '----------------------------------
 1020 *START_DEMO
 1021   SCREEN 0:SKCLOSE:ACTIVE 5:KPRINT (10,200),"Test of the general graphics commands":ACTIVE 4:PRIORITY 4,1
 1022   WIDTH 1,1,38,26:COLOR ,RGB(31,31,31)
 1023   VOLUME 111:BGM 1
 1024 '
 1025 '==========================================================
 1026 '●[PSET,LINE,CIRCLE] DEMO
 1027 '==========================================================
 1028 FOR J=0 TO 20000
 1029   PSET(RND(320),RND(199)),RND(32768)
 1030 NEXT
 1031 '
 1032 FOR J=0 TO 10000
 1033   LINE (RND(320),RND(199))-(RND(320),RND(199)),RND(32768)
 1034 NEXT
 1035 '
 1036 FOR J=0 TO 5000
 1037   LINE (RND(320),RND(199))-(RND(320),RND(199)),RND(32768),B
 1038 NEXT
 1039 '
 1040 FOR J=0 TO 1000
 1041   LINE (RND(320),RND(199))-(RND(320),RND(199)),RND(32768),BF
 1042 NEXT
 1043 '
 1044 FOR J=0 TO 5000
 1045   CIRCLE(RND(320),RND(199)),RND(120),RND(32768)
 1046 NEXT
 1047 '
 1048 FOR J=0 TO 1000
 1049   CIRCLE(RND(320),RND(199)),RND(120),RND(32768),F
 1050 NEXT

 1065    OBJ(I,XRV)=RND(16)/1024,RND(16)/1024,RND(16)/1024
 1066  NEXT
 1067  OBJ(1,TYPE)=4
 1068  OBJ(1,XP)=0,224,0
 1069  OBJ(1,YRV)=&h0.01

 1198 '==========================================================
 1199 '●TEXMAP.B texture draw test (motos)
 1200 '==========================================================
 1201 SCREEN 0,,,-1:KPRINT (10,200),"Use graphics commands on textures!"
 1202 TXSIZE=80:TXSIZ2=TXSIZE/2: 'Texture SIZE: multiple of 8
 1203 RESTORE *INDE_VERTEX: SETVERTEX  0,8,READ,(TXSIZ2,TXSIZ2,TXSIZ2)
 1204 RESTORE *INDE_POLYGON:SETPOLYGON 0,6,0,READ
 1205 SETATR 0,6 :'Reserve it first
 1206 FOR TX=0 TO 5
 1207   SETTEX TX,TXSIZE,TXSIZE,32768 :'Allocate the texture
 1208   CLS 10+TX             :'Delete the texture
 1209   '       t, f, s, t,  c, m
 1210   SETATR (0, 1, 3, TX,  0, 8):' Assign the texture to the attribute
 1211 NEXT TX
 1212 OBJ(1,ATR)  = 0,0       :' Link the attribute and polygon to the OBJ
 1213 OBJ(1,TYPE) = 4 :' POLYGON
 1214 OBJ(1,XRV) = .0009, .001:' Rotation speed
 1215 OBJ(1,XS)=1.5,1.5,1.5   :' Scale factor
 1216 '
 1217 ON INTERVAL (0) GOSUB *DRAW_LINE
 1218 ON INTERVAL (1) GOSUB *DRAW_BOXF
 1219 ON INTERVAL (2) GOSUB *DRAW_BOX
 1220 ON INTERVAL (3) GOSUB *DRAW_CIRCLE
 1221 ON INTERVAL (4) GOSUB *DRAW_ELLIPSE
 1222 ON INTERVAL (5) GOSUB *RANDOM_PAINT
 1223 INTERVAL (0) ON,1:INTERVAL (1) ON,1:INTERVAL (2) ON,1
 1224 INTERVAL (3) ON,1:INTERVAL (4) ON,1:INTERVAL (5) ON,1
 1225 VSYNC 60*5
 1226 INTERVAL (0) OFF:INTERVAL (1) OFF:INTERVAL (2) OFF
 1227 INTERVAL (3) OFF:INTERVAL (4) OFF:INTERVAL (5) OFF
 1228 GOTO *NEKO
 1229 '
 1230 *DRAW_LINE:   LOCK :ACTIVE 10
 1231  FOR N1=1 TO 4
 1232    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(128),RND(128),RND(256))
 1233  NEXT N1
 1234  UNLOCK :RETURN
 1235 '
 1236 *DRAW_BOXF:   LOCK :ACTIVE 12
 1237  FOR N2=1 TO 3
 1238    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(128),RND(256),RND(128)),BF
 1239  NEXT N2
 1240  UNLOCK :RETURN
 1241 '
 1242 *DRAW_BOX:    LOCK :ACTIVE 11
 1243  FOR N3=1 TO 4
 1244    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(128)),B
 1245  NEXT N3
 1246  UNLOCK :RETURN
 1247 '
 1248 *DRAW_CIRCLE: LOCK :ACTIVE 13
 1249  FOR N4=1 TO 2
 1250    CIRCLE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RND(TXSIZ2),RGB(RND(128),RND(256),RND(256)),F
 1251  NEXT N4
 1252  UNLOCK :RETURN
 1253 '
 1254 *DRAW_ELLIPSE:LOCK :ACTIVE 14
 1255  FOR N5=1 TO 2
 1256    CIRCLE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),(RND(20),RND(20)),RGB(RND(256),RND(128),RND(256)),F
 1257  NEXT N5
 1258  UNLOCK :RETURN
 1259 '
 1260 *RANDOM_PAINT:LOCK :ACTIVE 15
 1261  PC=PC+1
 1262  IF PC < 5 THEN
 1263    CIRCLE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RND(TXSIZ2),RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(256))
 1264    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(256)),B
 1265  ELSE
 1266    IF PC < 20 THEN
 1267      PX = RND(TXSIZE): PY = RND(TXSIZE)
 1268      IF POINT(PX,PY) < 0 THEN PAINT (PX,PY) ON RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(256))
 1269    ELSE
 1270      PC = 0
 1271      LINE (0,0)-(TXSIZE,TXSIZE),-1,BF:' It gets clipped, so any value will do
 1272    ENDIF
 1273  ENDIF
 1274  UNLOCK :RETURN
 1275 '
 1276 '==========================================================
 1277 '●2D sprite display sample
 1278 ' Written by Kanayama (motos)
 1279 '==========================================================
 1280 *NEKO
 1281 SCREEN 0
 1282 KPRINT (10,20,0,1,0)
 1283 KPRINT "           Sound features",,,RGB(20,0,20)
 1284 KPRINT "                                     "
 1285 KPRINT "     32 channels / 16 tracks"
 1286 KPRINT "          DSP effector"
 1287 KPRINT "         Pitch bend"
 1288 KPRINT "       Loop structures as in musical notation"
 1289 KPRINT "              Key change"
 1290 KPRINT "            Chord playing"
 1291 KPRINT "     ALFO/PLFO/envelope control"
 1292 KPRINT "                                     "
 1293 KPRINT "                                     "
 1294 VSYNC 60*4
 1295 SCREEN 0: PRIORITY 10,1 :'Put sprites behind the text screen
 1296 KPRINT (120,40),"<- Sprite type 1"
 1297 KPRINT (128,70),"Sprite type 2 (down)"
 1298 KPRINT (18,200),"(up) Sprite type 3"
 1299 TEX_NUM = 0   :'TEXTURE number to assign
 1300 TEX_HS  = 112 :'TEXTURE width size
 1301 TEX_VS  = 113 :'TEXTURE height size
 1302 ATR_NUM = 0   :'ATTRIBUTE number to assign
 1303 '
 1304 RESTORE *NEKO_PAL:PALETTE 10,0,READHEX$(256*2)          :'Read sprite color from DATA statement.
 1305 RESTORE *NEKO_TEX:SETTEX TEX_NUM,TEX_HS,TEX_VS,256,READ :'Read texture pattern from DATA statement.
 1306 SETATR ATR_NUM,1,(0, 1, 3, TEX_NUM, 0, 0)
 1307 ' A sprite's Z position is used as the display priority between sprites.
 1308 ' If it is beyond 100 it may not be displayed at all.
 1309 '
 1310 OBJ(1,TYPE) = 1: 'Z-rotation sprite
 1311 OBJ(1,ATR)  = ATR_NUM
 1312 OBJ(1,XP)   = -100,-50,300 :' X,Y position given
 1313 '
 1314 OBJ(2,TYPE) = 2: 'Sprite with independent H/V scale
 1315 OBJ(2,ATR)  = ATR_NUM
 1316 OBJ(2,XP)   = 100,30,200 :' X,Y position given
 1317 '
 1318 OBJ(3,TYPE) = 3: '4-point sprite
 1319 OBJ(3,ATR)  = ATR_NUM
 1320 OBJ(3,XP)   = -70,50,100 :' X,Y,Z position given (reference position for the 4 points)
 1321 '
 1322 FOR TT=0 TO 6000
 1323  OBJ(1,ZR) = XSIN(N*3)/16    :'Tilt left and right
 1324  OBJ(1,XS) = XSIN(N/4)/4+.8  :'Scale slowly
 1325  OBJ(2,XS) = XSIN(N)/4+.8,XCOS(N)/4+.8 :'Give the left/right scale factors
 1326  P0_X = -TEX_HS/4 + XSIN(N*1.2)*50 : P0_Y = -TEX_VS/4 + XSIN(N)*10
 1327  P1_X = +TEX_HS/4 + XCOS(N*1.2)*50 : P1_Y = -TEX_VS/4 + XCOS(N)*10
 1328  P2_X = +TEX_HS/4 + XSIN(N)*100: P2_Y = +TEX_VS/4 + XSIN(N*1.7)*10
 1329  P3_X = -TEX_HS/4 + XCOS(N)*100: P3_Y = +TEX_VS/4 + XCOS(N*1.7)*10
 1330  OBJ(3,X0) = P0_X,P0_Y, P1_X,P1_Y, P2_X,P2_Y, P3_X,P3_Y
 1331  N=(N+&H0.001) AND! &HFFFF.FFFC
 1332 NEXT
 1333 '
 1334 '

 1372 '==========================================================
 1373 '●AZ-1
 1374 '==========================================================
 1375 *INDEMO
 1376 SCREEN 0
 1377 KPRINT (10,20,0,1,0)
 1378 KPRINT "              General commands",,,RGB(20,0,20)
 1379 KPRINT "                                     "
 1380 KPRINT "      Fixed point for speed"
 1381 KPRINT "     Floating point too, of course"
 1382 KPRINT "                                     "
 1383 KPRINT "             Multi-dimensional arrays"
 1384 KPRINT "                                     "
 1385 KPRINT "        Labels, structured IF"
 1386 KPRINT "                                     "
 1387 KPRINT "                                     "
 1388 KPRINT "                                     "
 1389 VSYNC 60*4
 1390   SCREEN 0,,,-1:PRIORITY 10,1:KPRINT (10,200),"Process a digital-camera picture and"
 1391 '----------------------------------
 1392 '●Register AZ-1
 1393 '----------------------------------
 1394   SETLIGHT -1,1,1
 1395   RESTORE *INDE_VERTEX: SETVERTEX  0,8,READ
 1396   RESTORE *INDE_POLYGON:SETPOLYGON 0,6,0,READ
 1397   RESTORE *INDE_TEX:    SETTEX     0,296,250,32768,READ
 1398   SETATR   0,6,(0, 1, 3, 0, 0, 8)
 1399 '----------------------------------
 1400 '●Register AZ-1 as parent of the 3D cube
 1401 '----------------------------------
 1402   OBJ(2,ATR) = 0,0           :' Link the attribute and polygon to the OBJ
 1403   OBJ(2,TYPE)= 4             :' POLYGON
 1404   OBJ(2,XRV) = .002, .002    :' Rotation speed
 1405   OBJ(2,XS)  = 0,0,0         :' Scale factor
 1406 '----------------------------------
 1407 '●Parent AZ-1 appears while growing
 1408 '----------------------------------
 1409   FOR I=0 TO 60 STEP .2:OBJ(2,XS)=I,I,I:VSYNC:NEXT:KPRINT (10,200),"   it's fun stuck on a polygon too!"
 1410 '----------------------------------
 1411 '●Register 3 child AZ-1s
 1412 '----------------------------------
 1413   OBJ(3,ATR) = 0,0           :' Link the attribute and polygon to the OBJ
 1414   OBJ(3,TYPE)= 4             :' POLYGON
 1415   OBJ(3,XRV) = .001, .001    :' Rotation speed
 1416   OBJ(3,XS)  = 10,10,10      :' Scale factor
 1417   OBJ(3,20)  = 2             :' Parent-child relationship
 1418 '
 1419   OBJ(4,ATR) = 0,0           :' Link the attribute and polygon to the OBJ
 1420   OBJ(4,TYPE)= 4             :' POLYGON
 1421   OBJ(4,XRV) = .001, .001    :' Rotation speed
 1422   OBJ(4,XS)  = 10,10,10      :' Scale factor
 1423   OBJ(4,20)  = 2             :' Parent-child relationship
 1424 '
 1425   OBJ(5,ATR) = 0,0           :' Link the attribute and polygon to the OBJ
 1426   OBJ(5,TYPE)= 4             :' POLYGON
 1427   OBJ(5,XRV) = .001, .001    :' Rotation speed
 1428   OBJ(5,XS)  = 10,10,10      :' Scale factor
 1429   OBJ(5,20)  = 2             :' Parent-child relationship
 1430 '----------------------------------
 1431 '●Child AZ-1s appear
 1432 '----------------------------------
 1433   FOR H=0 TO 100 STEP .2
 1434     GOSUB *KO_INDE_POS:VSYNC
 1435   NEXT
 1436 '----------------------------------
 1437 '●Child AZ-1s rotate
 1438 '----------------------------------
 1439   AN_MAX=.02
 1440   FOR I=0 TO AN_MAX STEP .0001
 1441     GOSUB *KO_INDE_POS
 1442     AN=FRAC(AN+I)
 1443     VSYNC
 1444   NEXT
 1445 '----------------------------------
 1446 '●Keep going round forever (lol)
 1447 '----------------------------------
 1448   FOR TT=0 TO 60*10
 1449     GOSUB *KO_INDE_POS
 1450     AN=FRAC(AN+AN_MAX)
 1451     VSYNC
 1452   NEXT
 1453   GOTO *CAME
 1454 '----------------------------------
 1455 '●Subroutine to calculate child AZ-1 coordinates
 1456 '----------------------------------
 1457 *KO_INDE_POS
 1458   OBJ(3,XP)=XSIN(AN)*H,XCOS(AN)*H,0
 1459   OBJ(4,XP)=XSIN(AN-.25)*H,0,XCOS(AN+.25)*H
 1460   OBJ(5,XP)=0,XSIN(AN-.25)*H,XCOS(AN-.25)*H
 1461   RETURN
 1462 '

 1466 *CAME
 1467 SCREEN 0

 1484 RBG_PRIORITY=4

 1492 NEXT I

 1495 CCOPY 8,(0,0)-(127,127) TO 8,(128,128)

 1506 OBJ(4,XP)=40,CUBE_CENTER,0
 1507 OBJ(5,TYPE)=4
 1508 OBJ(5,XP)=30,CUBE_CENTER,50

 1515  OBJ(3,ZP)=XSIN(N*5)*280

 1537 *LOOK
 1538  HIGHT=XSIN(CZ)*VIEW_HEIGHT-VIEW_HEIGHT/2
 1539  IF HIGHT > 0 THEN PRIORITY 10,RBG_PRIORITY-1 ELSE PRIORITY 10,RBG_PRIORITY
 1540  CAMERA (XCOS(CZ*2)*500,HIGHT,XSIN(CZ*9)*320),-.04 TO TARGET,BG
```

### CLOCK.B: Clock

**File:** `CLOCK.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 96 bytes, 5 lines. Run it with `LOAD "CD:CLOCK.B",R`.

A five-line digital clock: it enlarges the text screen with `ZOOM` and prints the time from `DATE$` in a loop. It is the Tutorial Manual's first program (TM section 2.3).

**Techniques:**

- `ZOOM`, `LOCATE`, `RIGHT$(DATE$,18)` and a label loop

```
100 SCREEN 0
110 ZOOM 4,2,4
120 *LOOP
130   LOCATE 0,2:? RIGHT$(DATE$,18)
140 GOTO *LOOP
```

### P_CLOCK.B: Polygon clock

**File:** `P_CLOCK.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 999 bytes, 33 lines. Run it with `LOAD "CD:P_CLOCK.B",R`.

A digital clock made of polygon font characters. Each character of the time is a separate object. The Tutorial Manual explains it (TM section 2.6, "Displaying polygon fonts").

**Techniques:**

- `SETPFONT` to make 3D letters and digits
- The "Object Item Number" constants (`TYPE`, `XP`, `ATR`...) used with `OBJ(n,item)`
- Placing objects in a row centred on the screen

```
 1000 '----------------------------------
 1010 'Object Item Number
 1020 TYPE = 0: FLAG = 1
 1030 XP = 4: YP = 5: XR = 8: XS = 12
 1040 ATR = 16: POLYGON = 17: ORDER = 18
 1050 PARENT = 20: CHILD = 21
 1060 XV = 24: XA = 28: XL = 32: XRV= 36
 1070 '----------------------------------
 1080 SCREEN 0
 1090 GOSUB *SETFONT
 1100 *LOOP
 1120   TIME$=RIGHT$(DATE$,12)
 1130   FOR LN=1 TO LEN(TIME$)
 1140    CH$=MID$(TIME$,LN,1): CH=ASC(CH$)
 1150    IF CH$ >= "A" AND CH$ <= "Z" THEN CH2=CH-ASC("A")+10: GOTO *PUT
 1160    IF CH$ >= "0" AND CH$ <= "9" THEN CH2=CH-ASC("0"): GOTO *PUT
 1170    GOTO *NOCHR
 1180 *PUT
 1190    OBJ(LN,ATR)=CH2,CH2
 1200    OBJ(LN,TYPE)=4:OBJ(LN,PARENT)=0
 1210    OBJ(LN,XP)=(LN-1-LEN(TIME$)/2)*20
 1220 *NOCHR
 1230   NEXT LN
 1240   GOTO *LOOP
 1250 '
 1260 *SETFONT
 1270   FOR I=0 TO 9
 1280    SETPFONT ,ASC("0")+I,(.3,1,1)
 1290   NEXT I
 1300   FOR I=0 TO 25
 1310    SETPFONT ,ASC("A")+I,(.3,1,1)
 1320   NEXT I
 1330   RETURN
```

### P_PFONT.B: Polygon font test ("Alphabet Soup")

**File:** `P_PFONT.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 856 bytes, 26 lines. Run it with `LOAD "CD:P_PFONT.B",R`.

The 26 letters as polygon font objects, arranged in a ring around a parent object that spins. Explained in TM section 2.6.

**Techniques:**

- `SETPFONT` with colours from `RND`
- Parent-child objects: rotating the parent turns the whole ring
- `SETLIGHT`

```
 1000 SCREEN 0
 1010 '----------------------------------
 1020 'Object Item Number
 1030 TYPE = 0: FLAG = 1
 1040 XP = 4: YP = 5: XR = 8: YR = 9: ZR = 10: XS = 12
 1050 ATR = 16: POLYGON = 17: ORDER = 18
 1060 PARENT = 20: CHILD = 21
 1070 XV = 24: XA = 28: XL = 32: XRV= 36
 1080 '----------------------------------
 1090 PRINT "Alphabet Soup2..."
 1100 'SETLIGHT 0.7,0.01,0.1,RGB(10,0,30),RGB(3,3,3)
 1110 SETLIGHT 1,0,0
 1120 SETDISP 3
 1130 PRIORITY 10,1: OBJ(100,TYPE)=6
 1140 OBJ(100,XRV)=-.001,.0001,&H0.002
 1150 OBJ(100,XR)=-.17,.1
 1160 OBJ(100,XP)=-20,-70,110
 1170 '
 1180 FOR I=ASC("A") TO ASC("Z")
 1190  N=I-ASC("A")
 1200  OBJ(N+1,PARENT)=100: OBJ(N+1,TYPE)=4
 1210  OBJ(N+1,XRV)=.0008,.003
 1220  OBJ(N+1,XP)=XSIN(N/26)*250,XCOS(N/26)*250
 1230  SETPFONT N+1,I,,RGB(RND(32),RND(32),RND(32))
 1240 NEXT
 1250 '
```

### P_CAME2.B: Camera test

**File:** `P_CAME2.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 1,757 bytes, 58 lines. Run it with `LOAD "CD:P_CAME2.B",R`.

The camera circles over a rotating, scaling BG plane covered in random letters. Explained in TM section 2.6, "The camera".

**Techniques:**

- `CAMERA` and object 0 as the camera
- A rotation BG (`ROTZOOM`, `SETCHR`, `PUTCHR`) as the ground
- Circular motion with `XSIN`/`XCOS`

```
LOAD "COM:CAMERA2.B"
 1000 'Circular camera test with BG (motos)
 1010 SCREEN 5,4,256
 1020 PRINT "Camera with BG"
 1030 '----------------------------------
 1040 'Object Item Number
 1050 TYPE = 0: FLAG = 1
 1060 XP = 4: YP = 5: ZP = 6:XR = 8: YR = 9: ZR = 10: XS = 12
 1070 ATR = 16: POLYGON = 17: ORDER = 18
 1080 PARENT = 20: CHILD = 21
 1090 XV = 24: XA = 28: XL = 32: XRV= 36
 1100 '----------------------------------
 1110 ROTZOOM 2,2:  'Ground size
 1120 VIEW_HEIGHT=300
 1130 RBG_PRIORITY=4
 1140 PRIORITY 8,RBG_PRIORITY
 1150 A$=READCHR$(4,0,256)
 1160 SETCHR 8,0,A$
 1170 PALETTE 8,1,RGB(10,10,10)
 1180 PALETTE 8,15,RGB(0,30,30)
 1190 FOR I=1 TO 5000
 1200   PUTCHR 8,(RND(128),RND(128)),ASC("A")*2
 1210 NEXT I
 1220 CCOPY 8,(0,0)-(127,127) TO 8,(0,128)
 1230 CCOPY 8,(0,0)-(127,127) TO 8,(128,0)
 1240 CCOPY 8,(0,0)-(127,127) TO 8,(128,128)
 1250 '
 1260 CUBE_CENTER=-12
 1270 SETLIGHT -1,1,0
 1280 OBJ(1,TYPE)=4
 1290 OBJ(1,XP)=0,CUBE_CENTER,0
 1300 OBJ(2,TYPE)=4
 1310 OBJ(2,XP)=0,-100,0
 1320 OBJ(3,TYPE)=4
 1330 OBJ(3,XP)=-40,CUBE_CENTER,0
 1340 OBJ(4,TYPE)=4
 1350 OBJ(4,XP)=40,CUBE_CENTER,0
 1360 OBJ(5,TYPE)=4
 1370 OBJ(5,XP)=30,CUBE_CENTER,50
 1380 N=0
 1390 CX=80:CZ=0:CZV=-&H0.001
 1400 TARGET=3
 1410 SETDISP 3
 1420 *LOOP:VSYNC
 1430  OBJ(3,XP)=XCOS(N*4)*380
 1440  OBJ(3,ZP)=XSIN(N*5)*280
 1450  OBJ(3,XR+1)=.5-N
 1460  N=FRAC(N+&H0.002)
 1470  GOSUB *LOOK
 1480 GOTO *LOOP
 1490 *LOOK
 1500  HIGHT=XSIN(CZ)*VIEW_HEIGHT-VIEW_HEIGHT/2
 1510  IF HIGHT > 0 THEN PRIORITY 10,RBG_PRIORITY-1 ELSE PRIORITY 10,RBG_PRIORITY
 1520  CAMERA (XCOS(CZ*2)*500,HIGHT,XSIN(CZ*9)*320),-.04 TO TARGET,BG
 1530  CZ=FRAC(CZ+CZV)
 1540  IF 0 AND (CN > 10000) THEN CN=0
 1550 RETURN
'LOAD END
```

### P_SHOWER.B: Shower

**File:** `P_SHOWER.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 891 bytes, 30 lines. Run it with `LOAD "CD:P_SHOWER.B",R`.

A shower of polygon objects falling with random speeds and spins. The Tutorial Manual uses it as the example for sending a program from the PC (TM section 3.1, "Key send").

**Techniques:**

- Random object speed (`XV`) and rotation speed (`XRV`) so objects move by themselves
- `SETDISP`

```
LOAD "COM:D.B"
1000 SCREEN 0:SETDISP 1
1001 '----------------------------------
1002 'Object Item Number
1003 TYPE = 0: FLAG = 1
1004 XP = 4: YP = 5: ZP = 6
1005 XR = 8: YR = 9: ZR = 10
1006 XS = 12: XRV = 36: YRV = 37: ZRV = 38
1007 ATR = 16: POLYGON = 17: ORDER = 18
1008 PARENT = 20: CHILD = 21
1009 XV = 24: XA = 28: XL = 32: XRV= 36
1010 '----------------------------------
1011  *SETUP
1012  OBJ(0,ZP)=500
1013  FOR I=2 TO 100
1014    OBJ(I,TYPE)  =4
1015    OBJ(I,PARENT)=1
1016    OBJ(I,XP)=0,0,0
1017    OBJ(I,XR)=RND(1024)/1024,RND(1024)/1024,RND(1024)/1024
1018    OBJ(I,XL)=4,16,4
1019    OBJ(I,XV)=(RND(128)-64)/32,-(RND(128)+128)/32,(RND(128)-64)/32
1020    OBJ(I,XA)=0,&h0.0E,0
1021    OBJ(I,XRV)=RND(16)/1024,RND(16)/1024,RND(16)/1024
1022  NEXT
1023  OBJ(1,TYPE)=4
1024  OBJ(1,XP)=0,224,0
1025  OBJ(1,YRV)=&h0.01
1026  VSYNC 60*4:GOTO  *SETUP


```

### P_TEXMAP.B: Texture drawing test

**File:** `P_TEXMAP.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 3,347 bytes, 109 lines. 97 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:P_TEXMAP.B",R`.

Draws on a texture with ordinary graphics commands while the texture is shown on a spinning polygon, so the picture changes as it turns.

**Techniques:**

- Making a texture and drawing into it with `LINE`, `CIRCLE` and `PAINT`
- `ON INTERVAL` to keep drawing
- Linking attribute and polygon to an object

```
LOAD "COM:TEXMAP.B"
1000 'Texture draw test (motos)
1010 '
1020 SCREEN 0,,,-1
1030 '----------------------------------
1040 'Object Item Number
1050 TYPE = 0: FLAG = 1
1060 XP = 4: XR = 8: XS = 12
1070 ATR = 16: POLYGON = 17: ORDER = 18
1080 PARENT = 20: CHILD = 21
1090 XV = 24: XA = 28: XL = 32: XRV= 36
1100 '----------------------------------
1110 TXSIZE=80:TXSIZ2=TXSIZE/2: 'Texture SIZE: multiple of 8
1120 SETVERTEX  0,8,READ,(TXSIZ2,TXSIZ2,TXSIZ2)
1130 SETPOLYGON 0,6,0,READ
1140 SETATR 0,6 :'Reserve it first
1150 FOR TX=0 TO 5
1160   SETTEX TX,TXSIZE,TXSIZE,32768 :'Allocate the texture
1170   CLS 10+TX             :'Delete the texture
1180   '       t, f, s, t,  c, m
1190   SETATR (0, 1, 3, TX,  0, 8):' Assign the texture to the attribute
1200 NEXT TX
1210 OBJ(1,ATR)  = 0,0       :' Link the attribute and polygon to the OBJ
1220 OBJ(1,TYPE) = 4 :' POLYGON
1230 OBJ(1,XRV) = .0009, .001:' Rotation speed
1240 OBJ(1,XS)=1.5,1.5,1.5   :' Scale factor
1250 '
1260 ON INTERVAL (0) GOSUB *DRAW_LINE
1270 ON INTERVAL (1) GOSUB *DRAW_BOXF
1280 ON INTERVAL (2) GOSUB *DRAW_BOX
1290 ON INTERVAL (3) GOSUB *DRAW_CIRCLE
1300 ON INTERVAL (4) GOSUB *DRAW_ELLIPSE
1310 ON INTERVAL (5) GOSUB *RANDOM_PAINT
1320 INTERVAL (0) ON,1
1330 INTERVAL (1) ON,1
1340 INTERVAL (2) ON,1
1350 INTERVAL (3) ON,1
1360 INTERVAL (4) ON,1
1370 INTERVAL (5) ON,1
1380 '
1390 *LOOP:GOTO *LOOP
1400 END
1410 '
1420 '==== VERTEX
1430 DATA -1, -1,-1
1440 DATA  1, -1,-1
1450 DATA  1,  1,-1
      ' ... 10 DATA lines and 2 comment lines not shown (lines 1460-1570) ...
1580 DATA , (2, 7, 6, 3)
1590 '
1600 *DRAW_LINE:   LOCK :ACTIVE 10
1610  FOR N1=1 TO 4
1620    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(128),RND(128),RND(256))
1630  NEXT N1
1640  UNLOCK :RETURN
1650 '
1660 *DRAW_BOXF:   LOCK :ACTIVE 12
1670  FOR N2=1 TO 3
1680    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(128),RND(256),RND(128)),BF
1690  NEXT N2
1700  UNLOCK :RETURN
1710 '
1720 *DRAW_BOX:    LOCK :ACTIVE 11
1730  FOR N3=1 TO 4
1740    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(128)),B
1750  NEXT N3
1760  UNLOCK :RETURN
1770 '
1780 *DRAW_CIRCLE: LOCK :ACTIVE 13
1790  FOR N4=1 TO 2
1800    CIRCLE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RND(TXSIZ2),RGB(RND(128),RND(256),RND(256)),F
1810  NEXT N4
1820  UNLOCK :RETURN
1830 '
1840 *DRAW_ELLIPSE:LOCK :ACTIVE 14
1850  FOR N5=1 TO 2
1860    CIRCLE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),(RND(20),RND(20)),RGB(RND(256),RND(128),RND(256)),F
1870  NEXT N5
1880  UNLOCK :RETURN
1890 '
1900 *RANDOM_PAINT:LOCK :ACTIVE 15
1910  PC=PC+1
1920  IF PC < 5 THEN
1930    CIRCLE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RND(TXSIZ2),RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(256))
1940    LINE (RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE))-(RND(TXSIZE),RND(TXSIZE)),RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(256)),B
1950  ELSE
1960    IF PC < 20 THEN
1970      PX = RND(TXSIZE): PY = RND(TXSIZE)
1980      IF POINT(PX,PY) < 0 THEN PAINT (PX,PY) ON RGB(RND(256),RND(256),RND(256))
1990    ELSE
2000      PC = 0
2010      LINE (0,0)-(TXSIZE,TXSIZE),-1,BF:' It gets clipped, so any value will do
2020    ENDIF
2030  ENDIF
2040  UNLOCK :RETURN
'LOAD END


```

### P_FLOWER.B: Texture display test

**File:** `P_FLOWER.B` on the GAME BASIC CD, 18,100 bytes, 277 lines. 27 lines shown. Run it with `LOAD "CD:P_FLOWER.B",R`.

A textured flower picture on a polygon, with several copies linked to it and turning.

**Techniques:**

- `PALETTE ... READHEX$` to load a 256-colour palette from `DATA`
- `SETTEX`, `SETVERTEX`, `SETPOLYGON`, `SETATR`
- The `OBJATR`, `OBJTYPE`, `OBJTURN`, `OBJLINK` commands

```
1000 'Texture display sample (motos)

1070 SETATR     1,1,(0,1,2,0,0,0)
1080 OBJATR  1,1,1
1090 OBJTYPE 1,4
1100 OBJTURN 1,,&H0.001,-&H0.004
1110 FOR N=2 TO 2+6
1120  OBJATR  N,1,1
1130  OBJLINK N,1
1140  ANGLE=N/6:DIST=70
1150  OBJPOS  N,XSIN(ANGLE)*DIST,XCOS(ANGLE)*DIST,2
1160  OBJTYPE N,4
1170  OBJ(N,18)=1
1180  OBJTURN N,,-&H0.001,&H0.004
1190 NEXT
1200 END
```
